He has personally borne our griefs, carried our sorrows, and taken upon Himself our pains and sicknesses. He sends the Holy Ghost to comfort us, and the fruits of the Spirit include joy, peace, and faith, which fill us with hope and love.

speaker: Elder Benjamin M. Z. Tai
title: The Love of God
quote: To help others feel God’s love, we need to cultivate in ourselves Christlike attributes such as humility, charity, compassion, and patience and help turn others towards the Savior through following the two great commandments of loving God and loving our fellow men.

speaker: President Russell M. Nelson
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Confidence in the Presence of God
quote: The Lord has told us to “remember faith, virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, brotherly kindness, godliness, charity, humility, [and] diligence” (Doctrine and Covenants 4:6). When we do, our confidence will increase, and then, in His own words, when we ask, we shall receive. And when we knock, it shall be opened unto us. (See Doctrine and Covenants 4:7.)

speaker: President Russell M. Nelson
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Confidence in the Presence of God
quote: I am especially inspired by our youth. They are giving service in large numbers. They are seeking their ancestors and performing ordinances in the temple. Our young men and women are submitting applications for missionary service in record numbers. The rising generation is rising up as stalwart followers of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
quote: Gratefully, our young men and women are similarly drawn to their Sermon-on-the-Mount moments: seminary, For the Strength of Youth conferences, and Come, Follow Me. Here they receive the same enduring invitations from the Lord: to let their light shine before others, to seek righteousness even when persecuted, and to love their enemies.

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
quote: The hearts of today’s rising generation are filled with a testimony of Jesus Christ and a hope for the future. Yet they too ask, “Can I truly become a peacemaker when the world is in commotion, my heart is filled with fear, and peace seems so far away?”

speaker: Sister Tracy Y. Browning
role: Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency
title: Tune Your Heart to Jesus Christ: The Sacred Gift of Primary Music
quote: “Teach your children to love the hymns. Sing them on the Sabbath, in home evening, during scripture study, at prayer time. Sing as you work, as you play, and as you travel together. Sing hymns as lullabies to build faith and testimony in your young ones” (“First Presidency Preface,” Hymns, ix, x).

speaker: Sister Tracy Y. Browning
role: Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency
title: Tune Your Heart to Jesus Christ: The Sacred Gift of Primary Music
quote: Adult members across the globe, in times of difficulty, often remember and turn to the Primary songs they learned as children. For many, these songs supported the early architecture of their faith in Jesus Christ and were often the first place where conversion to His gospel began. Parents, leaders, and teachers nurtured that faith through the years by teaching, singing, and testifying to children with care.

speaker: Elder Ronald M. Barcellos
title: The Lord Looketh on the Heart
quote: The Savior taught, “If ye love me, keep my commandments⁠.” He invites us to demonstrate our love by making and keeping covenants with Him. As we strive daily to keep His commandments, sincerely repent from our sins, and persevere in taking His name upon us and aligning our will with His will, we can be blessed with the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost.

speaker: Elder Ronald M. Barcellos
title: The Lord Looketh on the Heart
quote: The Lord admonished Oliver Cowdery to “treasure up these words in thy heart.” We’re invited to search the scriptures diligently and, through the power of the Holy Ghost, seek to obtain understanding and a witness of the truthfulness of the gospel in our hearts.

speaker: Elder Brik V. Eyre
title: Know Who You Really Are
quote: In a worldwide devotional for young adults, our beloved President Russell M. Nelson taught: “So who are you? First and foremost, you are a child of God, a child of the covenant, and a disciple of Jesus Christ. As you embrace these truths, our Heavenly Father will help you reach your ultimate goal of living eternally in His holy presence.”

speaker: Elder Brik V. Eyre
title: Know Who You Really Are
quote: The greatest manifestation of Heavenly Father’s love for us as His children is the reality that He sent His Son, our own personal Savior, to help us come home. Therefore, we need to come to know Him.

speaker: Elder Kelly R. Johnson
title: Be Reconciled to God
quote: How does the Savior help us restore and reconcile this important relationship? For me, I make great progress in my journey to be reconciled to God when I follow the counsel taught by President Nelson and repent every day. The reason being that reconciliation signifies the restoration of a broken relationship, particularly between God and humanity, by removing the barrier of sin.

speaker: Elder Kelly R. Johnson
title: Be Reconciled to God
quote: Reconciliation brings not only relief from feelings of guilt but also peace within ourselves and with others. It heals relationships, softens hearts, and strengthens our discipleship, bringing increased confidence before God. What brings me great hope and confidence is another fruit of reconciliation described by Enos when he said, “And after I, Enos, had heard these words, my faith began to be unshaken in the Lord.”

speaker: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Do Your Part with All Your Heart
quote: Oh, how I wish I could embrace you and help you understand this great truth: You are a blessed being of light, the spirit child of an infinite God! And you bear within you a potential beyond your own capacity to imagine.

speaker: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Do Your Part with All Your Heart
quote: My beloved brothers and sisters, dear friends, I pray that the Spirit will help you recognize the gifts and talents God has given you. Then, let us, like the faithful servants in the Lord’s parable, increase and magnify them.

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Family Proclamation—Words from God
quote: Everyone belongs to a family, whether you are a mother, father, daughter, son, grandchild, grandparent, aunt, uncle, brother, sister, or cousin. Most importantly, each of us is, as the proclamation states, “a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents … [with] a divine nature and destiny.”

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Family Proclamation—Words from God
quote: The proclamation states, “Parents have a sacred duty to rear their children in love and righteousness.” The Book of Mormon provides a second witness to this truth. In the first verse of the first chapter, we read, “I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents.” How many of us have started the Book of Mormon—and started again and again—and in the process committed those words to memory? Commit them to heart.

speaker: Brother Chad H Webb
role: First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency
title: That All May Be Edified
quote: Today I invite you to consider the role of the Holy Ghost, specifically related to gospel learning and teaching in the home and at church. The Holy Ghost is given by the prayer of faith and as we strive to live worthy of this precious gift. The inspired Church manual Teaching in the Savior’s Way outlines additional principles the Lord has established that will help invite the influence of the Holy Ghost.

speaker: Brother Chad H Webb
role: First Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency
title: That All May Be Edified
quote: In our homes and Church meetings, as we focus on Jesus Christ, teach His doctrine, and learn diligently, we invite the Holy Ghost to deepen our faith in Jesus Christ and help us become more like Him, which is the aim of all gospel teaching and learning.

speaker: Elder Jeremy R. Jaggi
title: Humble Souls at Altars Kneel
quote: When we come to the altar, we aren’t earning a reward; we are learning about the Gift Giver. In that learning and covenant binding comes healing. Nephi said, “He hath filled me with his love, even unto the consuming of my flesh.” And our loving Savior invited, “Will ye not now return unto me, and repent of your sins, and be converted, that I may heal you?”

speaker: Elder Jeremy R. Jaggi
title: Humble Souls at Altars Kneel
quote: Building an understanding of the Savior’s eternal Atonement line upon line, precept upon precept, provides a spiritual inoculation against the wiles of the adversary. Young Elder Jaggi in Mexico, Zuster Jaggi in Belgium, and other missionaries throughout the world are much more likely to see their friends claim the blessings of baptism and receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost if their friends attend sacrament meeting within the first week of contact.

speaker: Elder Kevin G. Brown
title: The Eternal Gift of Testimony
quote: If you are a baptized and confirmed member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints but still struggle with “I am not sure if I know,” please remember this promise in the sacrament prayer: “That they may always have his Spirit to be with them.” Because of this promise, each of us can pursue the path to testimony and a sure knowledge.

speaker: Elder Kevin G. Brown
title: The Eternal Gift of Testimony
quote: My dear brothers and sisters, lately I have been reflecting on three powerful truths from the Restoration. These truths have profoundly blessed my life. Today, I would like to share with you how these truths have guided me on my journey toward a sure witness of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: No One Sits Alone
quote: I learn from faithful members and friends in every land and culture. Scriptures studied in multiple languages and cultural perspectives deepen gospel understanding. Different expressions of Christlike attributes deepen my love and understanding of my Savior. All are blessed when we define our cultural identity, as President Russell M. Nelson taught, as a child of God, a child of the covenant, a disciple of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: No One Sits Alone
quote: Covenant belonging deepens as we come to each other and to the Lord in His inn. The Lord blesses us all when no one sits alone. And who knows? Maybe the person we sit next to may become our best fortune cookie friend. May we find and make place for Him and each other at the supper of the Lamb, I humbly pray in the holy name of Jesus Christ, amen.

speaker: Elder Michael Cziesla
title: Simplicity in Christ
quote: Reference to the famous last sentence from Music & the Spoken Word, first introduced by Richard L. Evans: “Again we leave you from within the shadows of the everlasting hills. May peace be with you this day and always.”

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Lord Is Hastening His Work
quote: Learning the pure doctrine of Jesus Christ is a lifelong pursuit, both in understanding doctrine and living a Christlike life. Essential covenants provide a framework which we describe as the covenant path. These principles have been powerfully taught by President Nelson. All members, especially new and returning ones, would be blessed by studying and adopting his prophetic messages on covenants and the covenant path.

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Lord Is Hastening His Work
quote: We live in a turbulent time when “the whole earth [is] in commotion.” President Russell M. Nelson’s admonition to be peacemakers, as followers of Jesus Christ, was emphasized beautifully this morning by Elder Gary E. Stevenson. This is an essential part of fostering unity, peace, and healing for “the worst of times.”

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning
quote: Do you need a new beginning? Can you make a fresh start, even you? Think about the people the Saviour ministered to—the people He taught, healed, raised, forgave, and restored. Was He selecting them from a particular economic class or background? Was He distinguishing between the righteous and the sinful? Was He singling people out because they were more deserving or more loved? No.

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning
quote: “Our faith in Christ and our love for Him lead us to repent, or to change our thoughts, beliefs, and behaviors that are not in harmony with His will. Repentance includes forming a fresh view of God, ourselves, and the world” (Preach My Gospel: A Guide to Missionary Service [2004], 62).

speaker: Sister J. Anette Dennis
role: First Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
title: Cheering Each Other On
quote: Just like the Masters Championship, our congregations and families can be gathering places where we cheer each other on—covenant communities fueled by the love of Christ for one another—helping each other overcome whatever challenges we face, giving each other strength and encouragement without judging one another. We need each other. Divine strength comes from unity, and that is why Satan is intent on dividing us.

speaker: Sister J. Anette Dennis
role: First Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
title: Cheering Each Other On
quote: Christlike treatment of others goes far beyond our families and congregations. It includes our sisters and brothers of other faiths or no faith at all. It includes our brothers and sisters from other countries and cultures, as well as those of different political persuasions. We are all part of the family of God, and He loves all His children. He desires that His children love Him and also one another.

speaker: Elder Steven C. Barlow
title: “Lovest Thou Me?”
quote: Our Heavenly Father and our Savior recognize our expressions of love for Them when we put Them first in our lives, serve one another, gratefully acknowledge every blessing from Them, and choose to obey and follow Them.

speaker: Elder Steven C. Barlow
title: “Lovest Thou Me?”
quote: In the parable of the prodigal son, the elder brother initially struggled to celebrate when his younger brother returned home after a period of poor choices and “wast[ing] his substance with riotous living.” The elder brother’s pride and self-righteousness kept him from embracing the joy of his brother’s repentant return. We also may let opportunities pass us by without letting our loved ones know, through our words and actions, of our sincere love for them.

speaker: Elder William K. Jackson
title: Remembering the Sheep
quote: Christ is the Good Shepherd. Each one of the flock is precious to Him. He patterned shepherding and taught us by word and deed the qualities of a good shepherd, including knowing your sheep by name, loving them, finding those that are lost, feeding, and, ultimately, leading them back home again. He expects us to do the same as His undershepherds.

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Atoning Love of Jesus Christ
quote: I testify of the love, the mercy, and the grace of our Savior and Redeemer. He lives. We are His; we are children of the covenant. As we believe in Him, follow Him, and trust Him, He will lift us from our sorrows and our sins. Then, beyond this mortal life, in our Father’s house, we will live with Him forever and ever. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Atoning Love of Jesus Christ
quote: Your increasing faith will make your prayers more sincere, your scripture study more meaningful, and your desires more exact in keeping God’s commandments.

speaker: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: And Now I See
quote: Jesus gave the first meaning to this exchange, telling His disciples that all this had happened “that the works of God should be made manifest.” Remember that twice in this narrative the Savior’s action was referred to as “anointing” the blind man’s eyes, an act to be completed by washing. This description of “the works of God [being] made manifest” could possibly suggest the unfolding of an ordinance.

speaker: Elder James E. Evanson
title: Go and Do Likewise
quote: Service missionary purpose statement: “Help others come unto Christ by serving with loving kindness as the Savior would. Minister in His name to the one through the power of the Holy Ghost and live as an example of faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, covenant keeping with God, and enduring to the end” (Missionary Standards for Disciples of Jesus Christ—Service Missionaries, 1.0, Gospel Library).

speaker: Elder James E. Evanson
title: Go and Do Likewise
quote: Missionaries of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints are modern-day examples of the good Samaritan that Christ invites us to become. I would like to highlight those missionaries who are called to service assignments. They are examples to us of how service (1) opens hearts to the gospel of Jesus Christ, (2) allows all of us to minister regardless of our circumstances, and (3) brings the power of Christ into our lives.

speaker: Elder Ulisses Soares
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Adorned with the Virtue of Temperance
quote: “And no one can assist in this work except he shall be humble and full of love, having faith, hope, and charity, being temperate in all things, whatsoever shall be entrusted to his care.”

speaker: Elder Ulisses Soares
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Adorned with the Virtue of Temperance
quote: My beloved brothers and sisters, I extend an earnest invitation to all of us to adorn our minds and hearts with the Christlike virtue of temperance as a sacred response to the prophetic call of our dear President Russell M. Nelson. As we strive with faith and diligence to weave temperance into our actions and words, I testify that we will strengthen and anchor our lives more securely upon the sure foundation of our Redeemer.

speaker: Elder Peter M. Johnson
title: The Power of Ministering to the One
quote: Sisters and brothers, thank you for your faithful devotion in coming unto Jesus Christ during these challenging times. You are wonderful; you are beautiful; you are each a child of God. It is my prayer that we will recognize the influence of the Holy Ghost as we become and help one another become truly devoted disciples of Jesus Christ and feel of His joy as we worship in the house of the Lord.

speaker: Elder Peter M. Johnson
title: The Power of Ministering to the One
quote: We learn of the power of ministering to the one with compassion from Christ’s Apostles Peter and John. You remember a certain man, lame from birth, lay daily at the gate of the temple asking for money. This man may have felt unimportant, alone, discouraged, and unseen. He may have felt he did not belong.

speaker: Elder D. Todd Christofferson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Look to God and Live
quote: “Much of the world does not believe this, but public opinion is not the arbiter of truth. The Lord has declared that no unchaste person will attain the celestial kingdom. … If you have been unchaste, I plead with you to repent. Come unto Christ and receive His promise of complete forgiveness as you fully repent of your sins [see Isaiah 1:16–18; Doctrine and Covenants 58:42–43].”

speaker: Elder D. Todd Christofferson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Look to God and Live
quote: We can see around us the fruits of looking to God and having His Spirit to be with us. For example, research has found that “spiritual development is associated with protection against depression and substance abuse, and with setting young adults up for healthier relationships, more purposeful work, and greater emotional resilience” (Cornelia Powers, “The New Spiritual Leader on Campus,” Atlantic, May 18, 2025, theatlantic.com).

speaker: Sister Andrea Muñoz Spannaus
role: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: Prophets of God
quote: The Book of Mormon describes the 2,060 stripling warriors as “men of truth and soberness, for they had been taught to keep the commandments of God and to walk uprightly before him.” These young men faithfully obeyed Helaman, who at that time was their military leader and also their prophet, and they recognized that their mothers had filled their hearts with truth and faith.

speaker: Sister Andrea Muñoz Spannaus
role: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: Prophets of God
quote: The world’s wickedness is growing, but the Church of Jesus Christ and His kingdom are stronger than ever. Zion is putting on its beautiful garments, and Christ’s throne will not fall. The Lord expects us to be strong in our testimonies, to be full of faith, and to repent daily. Our Savior, Jesus Christ, is counting on each of us to carry on His work.

speaker: Elder Henry B. Eyring
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Proved and Strengthened in Christ
quote: When we continue to have faith in Jesus Christ—even when things might feel impossible to us at the moment—we become spiritually stronger. The sacred scriptural records emphasize this truth.

speaker: Elder Henry B. Eyring
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Proved and Strengthened in Christ
quote: Moroni’s testimony was refined in loneliness, but it shines with light to guide all generations to seek our Father in Heaven and the Savior Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: They Are Their Own Judges
quote: I pray for the assistance of the Holy Ghost as we consider Heavenly Father’s plan of happiness and mercy, the Savior’s atoning role in the Father’s plan, and how we will “be accountable for [our] own sins in the day of judgment.”

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: They Are Their Own Judges
quote: If our desires have been for righteousness and our works good—meaning we have exercised faith in Jesus Christ, made and kept covenants with God, and repented of our sins—then the judgment bar will be pleasing. As Enos declared, we will “stand before [the Redeemer]; then shall [we] see his face with pleasure.” And at the last day we will “be rewarded unto righteousness.”

speaker: Elder B. Corey Cuvelier
title: The Name by Which Ye Are Called
quote: In the end, our identity isn’t defined by the world. But our discipleship is defined by the ordinances we receive, the covenants we keep, and the love we show to God and neighbor by simply doing good. As President Nelson taught, we are indeed children of God, children of the covenant, disciples of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder B. Corey Cuvelier
title: The Name by Which Ye Are Called
quote: Let us strive to follow Christ’s example, doing good and making discipleship a lifelong priority so that each time we interact with others, they will feel God’s love and the confirming power of the Holy Ghost. Then we may join my great-grandfather and millions of others who have declared, like the disciple Andrew, “We have found the Messias.”

speaker: Elder Matthew S. Holland
title: Forsake Not Your Own Mercy
quote: Miraculously, Jonah escapes death when a “great fish” the Lord “prepared” swallows him. But he languishes in that unbelievably dark and putrid place for three days, until he’s finally spit out on dry ground. He then accepts his call to Nineveh. Yet, when the city repents and is spared destruction, Jonah resents the mercy shown his enemies. God patiently teaches Jonah that He loves and seeks to rescue all His children.

speaker: Elder Matthew S. Holland
title: Forsake Not Your Own Mercy
quote: God commanded Jonah to “go to Nineveh” to declare repentance. But Nineveh was ancient Israel’s brutal enemy—so Jonah promptly heads the exact opposite direction, by boat, to Tarshish. As he sails away from his calling, a ship-wrecking storm develops. Certain his disobedience is the cause, Jonah volunteers to be thrown overboard. This calms the raging sea, which saves his shipmates.

speaker: Elder Carlos A. Godoy
title: Smiling Faces and Grateful Hearts
quote: My new assignment took Monica and me to beautiful Africa, where the Church is flourishing. It has been a blessing to serve among the faithful Saints in the Africa South Area and witness the Lord’s love for them. It’s inspiring to see generational families of all backgrounds, including many successful and well-educated Church members, dedicating their time and talents to serve others.

speaker: Elder Carlos A. Godoy
title: Smiling Faces and Grateful Hearts
quote: Mpho Aniciah Nku, 14, a surviving accident victim in this picture, illustrated it well in her own words: “Trust in Jesus and always look unto Him, because through Him you’ll find peace, and He will help you in the healing process.”

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Taking on the Name of Jesus Christ
quote: The first parallel is identification. Dr. Selzman’s appointment to the Nelson professorship linked his name to President Nelson’s, and Dr. Selzman began to identify with President Nelson. When we take upon ourselves the name of Jesus Christ, we link our name with His. We identify with Him. We gladly become known as Christian. We acknowledge the Savior and unapologetically stand up to be counted as His.

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Taking on the Name of Jesus Christ
quote: The word ethos describes “the distinguishing character, sentiment, moral nature, or guiding beliefs of a person, group, or institution” (Merriam-Webster.com Dictionary, “ethos”).

speaker: Elder John D. Amos
title: The Good News Recipe
quote: If you have ever visited my home state of Louisiana, you are probably familiar with many of our tasty dishes—gumbo, jambalaya, étouffée, and the list goes on and on.

speaker: Elder John D. Amos
title: The Good News Recipe
quote: What do you do if something goes wrong when following the recipe? Well, embedded in the Good News Recipe is the “secret ingredient” to ensure you always get it right in the end. The answer is always Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Ozani Farias
title: The Book of Mormon—an Immeasurable Treasure on Our Journey
quote: Two weeks before Sister Benson completed her mission, her brother received his mission call. He is now serving in the Mexico Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mission. Through the Book of Mormon, Elder Benson came to see his life with spiritual clarity, which led him to serve the Lord and trust that things would work out. That decision was a miracle—influenced by the power of the words of Christ.

speaker: Elder Ozani Farias
title: The Book of Mormon—an Immeasurable Treasure on Our Journey
quote: Just as Lehi desired to share the fruit of the tree of life with his family (see 1 Nephi 8:12), when we gain a testimony of the Book of Mormon, we develop a desire to share the joy that comes from knowing the gospel of Jesus Christ.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ
quote: Parents also have a duty to teach their children practical knowledge apart from gospel principles. Families unite when they do meaningful things together. Family gardens build family relationships. Happy family experiences strengthen family ties. Camping, sports activities, and other recreation are especially valuable to bond families. Families should organize family reunions to remember ancestors, which lead to the temple.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ
quote: Parents should educate children in the basic skills of living, including working in the yard and home. Learning languages is a useful preparation for missionary service and modern life. The teachers of these subjects can be parents or grandparents or members of the extended family. Families flourish when they learn as a group and counsel together on all matters of concern to the family and its members.

speaker: Presented by President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: Solemn Assembly
quote: Please express your support in the usual way with the uplifted hand. If there are those who oppose any of the proposals, we ask that you contact your stake president.

speaker: Presented by President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: Solemn Assembly
quote: Thank you, brothers and sisters, for your sustaining vote on behalf of these leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: About His Business
quote: Some callings are highly stretching, while others may leave us wondering, “Isn’t there more I could be asked to do?” You might serve in a very visible role for a time, only later to be called to quiet, unseen service—or to support those with less experience. When callings change in ways that deeply impact you or your family, it can require great faith and trust in the Lord while you adjust.

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: About His Business
quote: “It is not appropriate to aspire to specific callings in the Church (see Mark 10:42–45; Doctrine and Covenants 121:34–37). Nor do Church members ‘advance’ from one calling to another. After serving in one calling, they should not expect to receive a calling of greater responsibility or prominence. Serving faithfully in a calling is more important than what the calling is. The Lord honors the dedication of all who serve in His Church” (General Handbook, 30.0).

speaker: Sister Kristin M. Yee
role: Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
title: Ministering—“That Ye Love One Another; as I Have Loved You”
quote: Choosing to minister isn’t always convenient or comfortable. It requires sacrifice, faith, vulnerability, and trusting things will work out as we let God prevail. When we pause and choose to care for someone over something, His Spirit and love can enter in and we can receive the peace and perspective that we really need.

speaker: Sister Kristin M. Yee
role: Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
title: Ministering—“That Ye Love One Another; as I Have Loved You”
quote: When we choose to minister in our inspired assignments and our daily interactions, we are helping to bless someone’s father, someone’s sister, someone’s son. When we minister, we are helping to answer each other’s prayers. We are the Savior’s hands. Oh, how I am grateful for all those who have blessed families like mine by ministering with compassion.

speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Come Home
quote: President Oaks has also taught the importance of patience, service, and love in overcoming faith questions (see “Coming Closer to Jesus Christ”).

speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Come Home
quote: In my weekend assignments as a General Authority, I have repeatedly witnessed people finding their way home. It may not always have come quickly, but it happened—over and over again. Let me take you on just a few of those ministering visits.

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: All Who Have Endured Valiantly
quote: The second half of the statement emphasizes the ongoing nature of our spiritual transformation: “We believe all things, we hope all things, we have endured many things, and hope to be able to endure all things. If there is anything virtuous, lovely, or of good report or praiseworthy, we seek after these things.”

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: All Who Have Endured Valiantly
quote: Enduring to the end is the joyous quest of a lifetime—a pressing forward with faith in Jesus Christ in a gradual process of trusting in and receiving help from our Savior to become more like Him. As our love for Him grows ever stronger and deeper, we can be blessed to receive spiritual perspective, the Lord’s empowering grace, and exceedingly great and indescribable joy.

speaker: Elder Michael John U. Teh
title: Follow the Prophet; He Knows the Way
quote: To the rich young man, Jesus said, “Sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.” The young man did not know that the path he was asked to tread would lead him to “treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.”

speaker: Elder Michael John U. Teh
title: Follow the Prophet; He Knows the Way
quote: I am grateful for teachings received over the years that have helped me better follow the Savior. For my purpose today, I simply would like to focus on one. As the Primary song goes, “Follow the prophet; he knows the way.”

speaker: Elder Jorge T. Becerra
title: Tithing—Putting God First
quote: A double-minded person is one who is wavering, indecisive, or conflicted, someone who lacks commitment to a single purpose or belief. One way to overcome double-mindedness is to learn to put God first in our lives. Jesus Christ taught, “Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness” (Matthew 6:33; emphasis added).

speaker: Elder Jorge T. Becerra
title: Tithing—Putting God First
quote: “And then the angel spake, saying: This thing is a similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten of the Father, which is full of grace and truth” (Moses 5:5–7; emphasis added).

speaker: President Henry B. Eyring
role: First Counselor in the First Presidency
title: Prayers for Peace
quote: Opening the windows of heaven through fervent prayer does not require the use of many words or flowery language. Rather, the diligence in prayer which Heavenly Father requires of us is to “pour out [our] souls” in private places and have our hearts “drawn out in prayer unto him continually.”

speaker: President Henry B. Eyring
role: First Counselor in the First Presidency
title: Prayers for Peace
quote: My dear brothers and sisters, I am grateful to be with you at this time when we can remember again the Savior’s comfort to His Apostles, as He knew that He would have to leave them alone, without Him to lead, protect, and succor them in their perils.

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Lost Luggage, Redeemed Souls
quote: Consider your ministering assignment as “Christlike caring” of the Lord’s most treasured possessions, who at the end of their mortal journey can be claimed and redeemed by Him. I invite you to implement small acts of kindness and care into your ministering, becoming better ministers of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Lost Luggage, Redeemed Souls
quote: Unlike pieces of luggage, each of us is ultimately responsible for our decisions, beliefs, and actions, assisted by heavenly and earthly ministering angels. Therefore, as disciples of Jesus Christ, we rise with renewed determination to succor and care for those with whom we come in contact.

speaker: Elder Eduardo F. Ortega
title: Christ—Author and Finisher of Our Faith
quote: A personal testimony comes in response to our sincere and dedicated quest to want to know for ourselves and then to act upon the impressions and the knowledge received. This pattern is repeated within many faithful member families in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints around the world.

speaker: Elder Eduardo F. Ortega
title: Christ—Author and Finisher of Our Faith
quote: The prophet Nephi taught: “Wherefore, ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and of all men. Wherefore, if ye shall press forward, feasting upon the word of Christ, and endure to the end, behold, thus saith the Father: Ye shall have eternal life.”

speaker: Elder Wan-Liang Wu
title: “I Will Give Away All My Sins to Know Thee”
quote: The only way we can come to know our Heavenly Father and gain eternal life is by coming unto Christ and following Him. Coming unto Christ is much more than just learning of Christ. It includes faith and works; it means to be converted to Him and to His restored gospel. As we do so, we “will have greater happiness, hope, peace, and purpose” in this life.

speaker: Elder Wan-Liang Wu
title: “I Will Give Away All My Sins to Know Thee”
quote: If we have a sincere desire, being meek and lowly in heart, we can come to know the true God the Father and gain eternal life through His Son, Jesus Christ, for the power is in us—in choosing to believe and deciding to act accordingly.

speaker: Brother David J. Wunderli
role: First Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency
title: Jesus Christ Is Not Our Burden; He Is Our Relief
quote: The enemy of happiness wants to separate you from Jesus Christ. He will tempt you to remove the Savior from your life, enticing you to think that the road would be easier without Him, that the weight of His commandments is too great, that the path back is too long, that repentance is too hard. Know this: Satan is a liar. Jesus Christ is not the weight; He is the relief.

speaker: Brother David J. Wunderli
role: First Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency
title: Jesus Christ Is Not Our Burden; He Is Our Relief
quote: You keep Jesus Christ with you as you exercise faith in Him, trust Him, and turn to Him in sincere, daily repentance.

speaker: Elder Gérald Caussé
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Love All; Love Each
quote: Through Belle’s patience, personal kindness, and loving care, an astonishing transformation begins—one that starts deep within the Beast’s soul and ultimately changes even his outward appearance. The spell is broken, and the young prince is restored, bringing great joy to all who gather to celebrate their new king and queen.

speaker: Elder Gérald Caussé
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Love All; Love Each
quote: I have always enjoyed the tale of Beauty and the Beast—not only because it is set in France or because I can easily relate to Lumière’s lovely accent but because of the beautiful truth it illustrates.

speaker: Elder Brian J. Holmes
title: Jesus Christ Is the Way
quote: Just as the band tethered the blind runner to his guide, covenants bind us to our guide—Jesus Christ. Elder David A. Bednar taught, “The covenant connection we have with our Heavenly Father and His resurrected and living Son is the supernal source of perspective, hope, power, peace, and enduring joy.”

speaker: Elder Brian J. Holmes
title: Jesus Christ Is the Way
quote: Once we bind ourselves to our Savior through covenant, only we can sever the tie. Jesus never will. As we remain tightly bound to Him, He is bound to us. We can expect His power to bless us with strength and joy even when we are experiencing a steep stretch of life. But if we turn away, we have no such promise. Covenant blessings flow from ongoing faithfulness, not merely from past participation.

speaker: Elder Clement M. Matswagothata
title: He Knows You by Name
quote: When life feels unfair and confusing, in those dark moments when you are tempted to ask, “O God, where art thou?” please remember this powerful truth: He knows you. He who “descended below all things” knows how to heal your broken heart and make you whole again. Trust His promise that the sun will rise again for you and tomorrow will be better than today.

speaker: Elder Clement M. Matswagothata
title: He Knows You by Name
quote: To the Savior, we are never lost in the crowd. He knows how to reach us—through a hymn, a smile, a kind word, and sometimes through people we least expect. Just as that family prayed for me, there is someone praying for you.

speaker: Elder Ulisses Soares
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Jesus Christ—the True Vine
quote: We live in a world filled with many voices—voices that relentlessly seek our attention and offer persuasive messages and invitations. Some speak with eloquence and influence and are well intentioned in their desire to promote goodness. Others are attractive in appearance but lack substance. Still others are misleading and may even appear to be connected to Christ and His gospel.

speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Encounter at the Empty Tomb
quote: The Savior has entrusted each of us personally with sacred spiritual experiences and knowledge. Because of those experiences, we can see for ourselves the meaning of the empty tomb: that Jesus Christ lives and is actively blessing all who seek Him.

speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Encounter at the Empty Tomb
quote: Living the message of the risen Christ testifies of our devotion and love for our Savior. It may well be that our consistent, courageous, and humble acts of service and love for God and His children will speak far more eloquently and powerfully than we ever could through words alone.

speaker: President Emily Belle Freeman
title: Best Days and Worst Days
quote: I don’t know what your story looks like right now, if today is a best day or a worst day. But here is my advice for you. On that worst day with Greg several weeks ago, I opened my For the Strength of Youth guide, wondering if the eternal truths, invitations, and promised blessings from the guide could really help Greg and me find strength in Christ.

speaker: President Emily Belle Freeman
title: Best Days and Worst Days
quote: Joseph Smith experienced something similar when he feared man more than God. On that day he was reminded of the importance of continuing in faith and then received these words from the Lord: “Behold, thou art Joseph, and thou wast chosen to do the work of the Lord. … Repent of that which thou hast done … [;] thou art still chosen, and art again called to the work” (Doctrine and Covenants 3:9, 10).

speaker: Elder Pedro X. Larreal
title: I Feel My Savior’s Love
quote: My dear brothers and sisters, do you know how much the Savior loves you? If you do not know or have never thought about it before, I hope by the end of this message you will know how to find the answer to this question.

speaker: Elder Pedro X. Larreal
title: I Feel My Savior’s Love
quote: The sacrament represents the Atonement of Jesus Christ. During that sacred moment, when we give our full attention to Him and focus on His atoning sacrifice, how can we not feel His great love for us? How can we not feel important when we remember that He willingly volunteered to be the Advocate between us and the Father?

speaker: Elder Edward B. Rowe
title: Choose Jesus Christ as Your Guide
quote: We will feel the Savior’s love, be blessed with His strength, and have greater trust in Him. Even our very natures will change to become more like Him. We will feel more joy. And our love and gratitude for Him will grow.

speaker: Elder Edward B. Rowe
title: Choose Jesus Christ as Your Guide
quote: Though our paths in life are unique, each is to be within the covenant path. For that is Christ’s path. We enter that path and connect ourselves to Jesus Christ as our guide through exercising faith in Him, repenting, and making sacred promises, or covenants, with Him.

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: He Is Risen
quote: Jesus Christ is “the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob,” “the Almighty God” of the Old Testament, “the light of the world” of the New Testament, “the Messiah” and “Savior of the world” of the Book of Mormon and other latter-day revelation. He came, was crucified, and rose again.

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: He Is Risen
quote: Jesus Christ is more than a mortal first laid in a manger, more than a friend, teacher, rabbi, minister, or prophet. He is the Only Begotten Son of the Father. And by divine design, His Resurrection by His own godly power reunited His body and His spirit. What a majestic and monumental event in Father in Heaven’s eternal plan.

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Because of Jesus Christ
quote: Because Jesus Christ completed the Atonement, He has the power to help you along your earthly journey and to redeem you from death, both physical and spiritual. Celebrate the joyous message of Easter every day by reflecting every day on the blessings you receive because of Him. “Open wide your broken heart and let your Savior in!”

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Because of Jesus Christ
quote: The third article of faith states, “We believe that through the Atonement of Christ, all mankind may be saved, by obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Gospel.”

speaker: Elder Thierry K. Mutombo
title: The Joy of a Covenant Relationship with God
quote: We can grow in humility and strengthen our covenantal relationship with our Heavenly Father and our Savior Jesus Christ if we change our nature to become like a child, building our life on the rock, who is the Savior Jesus Christ, yielding in faith in Him, responding to the Holy Ghost’s direction to faithfully keep the covenants made with the Lord at our baptism and in the house of the Lord.

speaker: Elder Thierry K. Mutombo
title: The Joy of a Covenant Relationship with God
quote: The miracle Nathalie and I prayed for happened after we stood for the truth and the light that is in Jesus the Christ. We received a strong confirmation that Christ works miracles according to our faith in Him. Sometimes things do not work out in mortality as we hope, and sometimes we need the faith in Jesus Christ that all will work out in the end.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Alive in Christ
quote: Persons who seek to reduce human suffering and persons who work to promote understanding among different peoples are also important workers for peace. So are faithful mothers and fathers who lovingly care for their own children or shelter foster children and raise them in righteousness rather than leave them to be scarred and twisted by the sins of others.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Alive in Christ
quote: Years later, President Howard W. Hunter described this same love of God toward His children: “The world in which we live would benefit greatly if men and women everywhere would exercise the pure love of Christ, which is kind, meek, and lowly. … It has no place for bigotry, hatred, or violence. … It encourages diverse people to live together in Christian love regardless of religious belief, race, nationality, financial standing, education, or culture.”

speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: The Character of Christ
quote: In the case of King Benjamin’s people, and some others, this spiritual rebirth with a changed heart was almost instantaneous. For most of us, our mighty change of heart occurs incrementally over time. In either case, the outcome is the same and equally valid. And in all cases, it requires faith in Christ, repentance, a baptismal covenant of obedience, and the grace of Jesus Christ through the Holy Ghost.

speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: The Character of Christ
quote: The love of Christ yields character traits such as compassion, patience, a willingness to correct “when moved upon by the Holy Ghost,” and certainly a willingness to forgive.

speaker: Elder Chi Hong (Sam) Wong
title: Remember, Remember
quote: Keeping God’s commandments is a blessing, both temporal and spiritual. If we can endure to the end, we will dwell with Him in a state of never-ending happiness. Isn’t that amazingly wonderful! However, have you ever thought about what will happen if we do not keep His commandments?

speaker: Elder Chi Hong (Sam) Wong
title: Remember, Remember
quote: Elder David A. Bednar taught how we can secure that foundation in our lives: “The sacred covenants and ordinances of the Savior’s restored gospel can be compared to the anchor pins and steel rods used to connect a building to bedrock. Every time we faithfully receive, review, remember, and renew sacred covenants, our spiritual anchors are secured ever more firmly and steadfastly to the ‘rock’ of Jesus Christ.”

speaker: Elder Aaron T. Hall
title: I Glory in My Jesus
quote: In moments of joy and in our trials, let us be faithful, obey His commandments, honor our covenants, and patiently wait on the Lord.

speaker: Elder Aaron T. Hall
title: I Glory in My Jesus
quote: I glory in our Good Shepherd. He calls to us, gathers us, rescues us, and fills us with His love. I rejoice that we are His sheep and that He relentlessly works to bring us safely home.

speaker: President Susan H. Porter
title: “Here Am I, Send Me”
quote: A few months ago, Chloe and Eli, both 10, stood before a group of business leaders and spoke confidently about how their faith affects their everyday life. They shared that they think about the gospel every day. They pray for others and look for ways to help. Chloe and Eli taught adults what it means to be disciples of Jesus Christ.

speaker: President Susan H. Porter
title: “Here Am I, Send Me”
quote: When you strive to bring yourself and others closer to Jesus, you will receive blessings now and later. Today you can make choices that will help you change and grow now and prepare you for blessings of love and joy forever.

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey
quote: In much of the world, confidence in the lasting nature of marriage is eroding. In the gospel of Jesus Christ, we proclaim that “marriage between a man and a woman is ordained of God.” We believe in eternal marriage, we teach of eternal marriage, and we seek an eternal marriage.

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey
quote: We anticipate our marriage with faith and confidence because we conscientiously prepare for the covenants we make in the house of the Lord. In our youth, we strengthen our faith in Jesus Christ and keep His commandments, including the law of chastity, a law so many in the world have set aside. We take upon us the name of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Keys, Covenants, and Easter
quote: The appearance of the Savior to the Prophet Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery and the keys committed by Moses, Elias, and Elijah are central to the Restoration of the gospel of Jesus Christ in the latter days. The role of Elijah in restoring the priesthood keys of the sealing power is crucial in our journey of returning to our Father as a covenant people.

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Keys, Covenants, and Easter
quote: If I were a 17-year-old and had access only to the Bible, I would have been very confused. Who was this prophet Elijah? And what priesthood would he reveal? Why would the whole earth be wasted if the children did not turn their hearts to their fathers and remember the promises made to them?

speaker: Elder Taniela B. Wakolo
title: Come unto Christ—Together
quote: The temple stands as a symbol of hope, not pressure. The gospel of Jesus Christ is not a wedge to divide families but a bridge to unite them eternally. We must ensure that our discipleship reflects the Savior’s patience, His gentleness, and His perfect love. Temple sealings invite us into the divine order of God. Is it any wonder that the temple sealing is often described as the crowning ordinance?

speaker: Elder Taniela B. Wakolo
title: Come unto Christ—Together
quote: My dear brothers and sisters, many of you are from families yet to be sealed in the temple. Some of you who are listening are not members of the Church. Others of you who are members of the Church may have spouses not of our faith. Today I say to each of you: You are essential to God’s plan.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: ’Tis Eastertide: No One Walks Alone
quote: Each Sabbath we invite all to come worship Jesus Christ in the community of His restored Church. In the sacramental ordinance, we covenant that we are willing to take upon us the name of Jesus Christ, always remember Him, and keep His commandments. He promises we can always have His Spirit to be with us. As we witness and remember Jesus each week, we abide and walk with Him.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: ’Tis Eastertide: No One Walks Alone
quote: With the disciples on the road to Emmaus, we sing: “Abide with me! fast falls the eventide; the darkness deepens. Lord, with me abide!” Continuing: “Earth’s joys grow dim; its glories pass away. Change and decay in all around I see; O thou who changest not, abide with me!” (“Abide with Me!,” Hymns, no. 166).

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Closing Remarks
quote: The Spirit of the Lord has inspired all of us to concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies on the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan for our eternal increase and joy.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Closing Remarks
quote: The Tabernacle Choir has just sung a musical prayer, “Tell Me the Stories of Jesus.” What a suitable summary of the messages of these last two days. Soon, we will close the conference with “Redeemer of Israel.” Both hymns continue the focus of the two days of this conference.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Come to the Lord in His Holy House
quote: So, why did the temple workers cross the road? So God and temple ordinances can protect, bless, and inspire; bring forgiveness, healing, and peace; and unite loved ones here and away. May these blessings of eternity be ours in even greater abundance, I pray, in the sacred name of Jesus Christ, amen.

speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Come to the Lord in His Holy House
quote: Today, as temples come closer in many places, we can manifest the precious spirit of temple sacrifice in new ways. We can come to the temple more often. We can search and bring more family names to bless deceased loved ones. As the seasons of our lives allow, we can regularly serve in the Lord’s house, both as temple patron and as temple ordinance worker.

speaker: Sister Tamara W. Runia
role: First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: The Sculpting of Our Souls
quote: C. S. Lewis explained, “God intends to give us what we need, not what we now think we want.” But sometimes we’re puzzled when we get what we need, aren’t we? How can our loving Father in Heaven watch as we go through heartbreaking experiences? I’ve wrestled with this, and maybe you have too.

speaker: Sister Tamara W. Runia
role: First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: The Sculpting of Our Souls
quote: When an angel asked Nephi, “Knowest thou the condescension of God?” he humbly answered, “I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things.”

speaker: Elder Gérald Caussé
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Gift of Testimony
quote: The truth of the restored gospel of Jesus Christ is manifest in the lives of millions of His followers throughout the world. Through your testimonies, in word and deed, you demonstrate the reality of a loving Savior and of the blessings that come through His gospel.

speaker: Elder Gérald Caussé
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: The Gift of Testimony
quote: The gift of testimony is deeply personal. It is received in the intimacy of our relationship with God and shaped according to our unique experiences, circumstances, and needs. It grows through faith, earnest seeking, gospel living, and the quiet influence of the Holy Ghost. Truly, “to know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God” is one of life’s greatest blessings and a precious gift from God.

speaker: Elder Vaiangina Sikahema
title: Prophets, Seers, and Revelators
quote: Joseph described the moment the heavens opened this way: “When the light rested upon me I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description, standing above me in the air. One of them spake unto me, calling me by name and said, pointing to the other—This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!” (Joseph Smith—History 1:17).

speaker: Elder Vaiangina Sikahema
title: Prophets, Seers, and Revelators
quote: How grateful I am for noble progenitors who left me and my posterity a legacy of faith and courage in the face of difficulties and obstacles.

speaker: Elder Kevin J. Hathaway
title: Jesus Christ Is the Great Deliverer!
quote: Sincere seeking means turning toward Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ through heartfelt prayer, purposeful fasting, and scripture study. Alma’s people in bondage “began to cry mightily to God.” King Darius fasted through the night as he waited for Daniel’s deliverance from the lions’ den. Such acts of faith draw us closer to Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Kevin J. Hathaway
title: Jesus Christ Is the Great Deliverer!
quote: Jesus Christ descended below all things and suffered “pains and afflictions and temptations of every kind”; therefore, He comprehends our suffering, is filled with mercy, and knows how to succor us according to our infirmities. With perfect understanding and infinite power, He can deliver the righteous from all things, forever. His deliverance is certain; the question for most righteous followers is not if He will deliver but how and when He will do so.

speaker: Elder Ulisses Soares
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: A Higher and Holier Fast
quote: What a tender promise: light after darkness, healing after weariness, and the comforting assurance that when we call upon the Lord, He is near. President Joseph F. Smith taught that proper fasting “would … place the body in subjection to the spirit, and so promote communion with the Holy Ghost” and that “this law would bring [us] nearer to God.”

speaker: Bishop Sean Douglas
role: Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
title: The Hour of Your Mission Is Come
quote: We rejoice exceedingly for your faithful response to the prophet’s call to action. Record numbers of missionaries of all ages are finding great joy as they humbly dedicate themselves to serving the Lord by laboring among Heavenly Father’s children. I wish to wholeheartedly add: There is still plenty of room and a special place reserved for each one of you! We need you! “Come join the ranks!”

speaker: Bishop Sean Douglas
role: Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
title: The Hour of Your Mission Is Come
quote: We love missionaries of all ages. You are an army of righteousness with the doctrine of Christ as your purpose. You are a force of faith, power, love, and joy. You are what you preach. You are not only the messengers but also living examples of the message. Make no mistake—you are doing the most important work you could be doing. We thank you for building up the kingdom of God on earth.

speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: O Be Wise
quote: Today I feel a bit like the Book of Mormon prophet Jacob, when he felt compelled by the Spirit to address subjects that were not particularly edifying, having to use “boldness of speech,” as he put it, instead of feasting on “the pleasing word of God.” So, with a sense of duty, I turn to the subject of gambling.

speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
role: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
title: O Be Wise
quote: Putting money or something of value at risk to bet on a particular outcome or event is an activity that has plagued mankind almost, I suppose, from the beginning of time. And time has not made it any more worthwhile or any less harmful. Unfortunately, in recent years, gambling has become incredibly pervasive.

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quote: Perhaps you have been served more than your share of cold oatmeal. Perhaps, like the children of Israel, you have doubted God’s care for you, His willingness to succor you, or His capacity to keep His promises. Yet God invites us to trust Him and His promises.

speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quote: One of the purposes of the Book of Mormon is to show us “what great things the Lord hath done … that [we] may know the covenants of the Lord, that [we] are not cast off forever.” Moroni exhorts us “that [we should] remember how merciful the Lord hath been unto the children of men [throughout the ages], and ponder it in [our] hearts.”

speaker: President Timothy L. Farnes
title: Divine Appointments
quote: Our promise of willingness is met by the Lord’s promise that we can always have His Spirit with us. With that gift, we can minister as the Savior would, with His power and His loving kindness.

speaker: President Timothy L. Farnes
title: Divine Appointments
quote: “Let your covenants guide your actions. When you have a choice to make, remember your covenant relationship with God. Be loyal to Him. Ask yourself: Does this align with my covenants? For example, do I love and minister to others, comfort people who need comfort, and stand as a witness of Christ—everywhere and always?” (For the Strength of Youth, 36).

speaker: Elder Christian C. Chigbundu
title: Spiritual Immunity
quote: My dear friends, I invite you to search the scriptures diligently, that you might know the word of God (see Alma 17:2). As we do this, little by little we learn how to become lifelong disciples of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Christian C. Chigbundu
title: Spiritual Immunity
quote: My beloved brothers and sisters, I invite you to always remember scriptures, prayers, the sacrament, and covenants. While they may seem small and simple, they are truly the armor of God that will help us stand against the tactics of the devil!

speaker: Elder Patricio M. Giuffra
title: Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings
quote: Throughout my life, I have learned to trust in the Lord, and I have seen innumerable blessings come to my family and me as we have sought to faithfully live the law of tithing and offerings. Some blessings have been temporal, others spiritual, but all have strengthened our testimony that the Lord always fulfills His promises and that the windows of heaven are opened according to our obedience.

speaker: Elder Patricio M. Giuffra
title: Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings
quote: President Dallin H. Oaks taught: “The payment of tithing … brings the individual tithe payer unique spiritual blessings. Tithe paying is evidence that we accept the law of sacrifice. It also prepares us for the law of consecration and the other higher laws of the celestial kingdom.” These laws are fulfilled as we keep the covenants made in the house of the Lord, which deepens and perpetuates our relationship with Jesus Christ.

speaker: Elder Jeremiah J. Morgan
title: The Infinite Power of God in Our Covenants
quote: Though the covenant faithfulness of parents and grandparents does not alter the agency of children or grandchildren, there is a discernible impact of those covenants on all our posterity.

speaker: Elder Jeremiah J. Morgan
title: The Infinite Power of God in Our Covenants
quote: If you are wondering whether you or a loved one has wandered so far away that the love of God and His covenantal power cannot reach you—I say to you, you have not. As President Jeffrey R. Holland so beautifully said: “You have not traveled beyond the reach of divine love. It is not possible for you to sink lower than the infinite light of Christ’s Atonement shines.”

speaker: Elder Hutch U. Fale
title: I Am a Child of God
quote: I bear solemn witness of the reality of this “plain and precious” truth, powerful and simple. Understanding our Father’s love and our true identity as His children is essential for our daily and eternal happiness. It prevents deception and gives purpose to this mortal life.

speaker: Elder Hutch U. Fale
title: I Am a Child of God
quote: “In the premortal realm, spirit sons and daughters knew and worshipped God as their Eternal Father and accepted His plan [for] His children.”

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Jesus Lives to Lift
quote: Through the amazing grace of Jesus Christ, we can avoid spiritual sink and find spiritual lift. Spiritual lift cannot be seen, but as we learn to discern and act upon the sensitive impressions of the Holy Spirit, we can feel it—as surely as I felt the rising air lift a wing beneath me.

speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Jesus Lives to Lift
quote: We can learn to live in spiritual lift. And when we sink, our gentle Saviour is there to lift us up as we turn to Him. Jesus Christ loves to lift!

speaker: Elder Michael A. Dunn
title: The Ninety and Ten
quote: Through “him who is mighty to save,” you will find “strength beyond [your] own.” In other words, don’t confuse the perceived invisibility of the Lord’s hand with the inveterate nature of the Lord’s heart. Peace will come even when hoped-for outcomes do not.

speaker: Elder Michael A. Dunn
title: The Ninety and Ten
quote: Among the myriad nearly incomprehensible blessings of our Savior Jesus Christ is His promise to carry our burdens. But what does that look like in practical terms—especially when we are weighed down and seemingly without hope?

speaker: Elder Matthew J. Eyring
title: Comfort from the Holy Ghost
quote: We have received repeated prophetic warnings that in coming days we will not survive spiritually without the constant influence of the Holy Ghost. One reason is that in a world of increasing temporal and spiritual turbulence, true sources of comfort will become more scarce. Without divine comfort, we risk losing hope; and without hope, we can lose our faith and stop trying. Our hearts can fail us.

speaker: Elder Matthew J. Eyring
title: Comfort from the Holy Ghost
quote: Someday we will more fully realize how generous and kind the Lord has been to each of us. We will better understand and appreciate the depth of the Savior’s sacrifice and the reality that He and the Father are truly givers of good gifts.

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Love Like Jesus
quote: For three long days and nights, young Alma “was racked with eternal torment.” Somewhere deep within came his father’s teachings of the coming of Jesus Christ “to atone for the sins of the world.” Alma cried in his heart, “O Jesus, thou Son of God, have mercy on me.” The love of the Savior filled him “with joy.” He became a mighty prophet and a major figure in the Book of Mormon.

speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Love Like Jesus
quote: President Dallin H. Oaks has counseled: “Let us avoid what is harsh and hateful. Let us seek to be holy, like our Savior.” That holiness comes when we are peacemakers, when we are charitable, patient, forgiving, and kind.

speaker: President Henry B. Eyring
role: First Counselor in the First Presidency
title: “Fear Not, I Am with Thee”
quote: You might reasonably wonder why a loving and all-powerful God allows our mortal test to be so hard. It is because He knows that we must grow in spiritual cleanliness and stature to be able to live in His presence. To make that possible, Heavenly Father gave us a Savior and the power to choose for ourselves by faith to keep His commandments and to repent and to come unto Him.

speaker: President Henry B. Eyring
role: First Counselor in the First Presidency
title: “Fear Not, I Am with Thee”
quote: You have prayed in faith consistently for your family members or friends to know who the Lord would have you help for Him. As a face or a name has come into your mind, you have reached out to them. Even your simple attention was a comfort. That you felt prompted to reach out to them was evidence to them that the Lord knew and loved them.

speaker: President Rosemary K. Chibota
title: A Child of God
quote: I plead with you as disciples of Jesus Christ to pray to see others as He sees them and to treat them accordingly. Remember, “Jesus said love ev’ryone; treat them kindly too.” When we see others through the Savior’s eyes, love and service naturally follow. President Spencer W. Kimball taught, “God does notice us, and … it is usually through another person that he meets our needs.”

speaker: President Rosemary K. Chibota
title: A Child of God
quote: The Savior Jesus Christ perfectly exemplified this principle. Throughout His ministry, He truly saw the people around Him. He saw the woman at the well, the leper, the blind man, and the child. Where others saw labels, He saw beloved sons and daughters of God. Even of the rich young man who later walked away from Him sorrowing, the scriptures say, “[And] Jesus beholding him loved him.”

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ
quote: Each week we prayerfully receive the sacrament and witness before God, and in the presence of others, that we “are willing to take upon [ourselves] the name of [Jesus Christ], and always remember him and keep his commandments.” Then, with courage, we are true to our covenants, and in turn, the Lord blesses us with increased faith.

speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ
quote: With faith in Christ and remarkable courage, a young mother prepares her small children for church, knowing that some Sundays will be more a wrestle of survival than a spiritual renewal.

speaker: Elder James G. O. Fantone
title: Take Upon Us His Name
quote: My beloved brothers and sisters, the Savior’s invitation is not for us to merely add His name to our names. His invitation is for us to take upon us His name by covenant and to serve Him with all our heart, might, mind, and strength—by lifting, loving, and serving our fellow men.

speaker: Elder James G. O. Fantone
title: Take Upon Us His Name
quote: How do we, as covenant children of God, truly take upon ourselves the name of Jesus Christ? How does that manifest in our daily lives?

speaker: Elder Edward Dube
role: Of the Presidency of the Seventy
title: Come unto Christ
quote: At the Childs’ home, following greetings and introductions, I empathized with his efforts to quit smoking. Then I asked, “Brother Child, how much do you love your wife, Laurin?”

speaker: Elder Edward Dube
role: Of the Presidency of the Seventy
title: Come unto Christ
quote: My humble invitation to us all: Will you find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ by exercising faith to follow His teachings, or invite a friend to meet with the missionaries?

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Integrity and Virtue Lead to Happiness
quote: Lifelong disciples of Jesus Christ best reflect the Savior’s teaching and direction when they joyfully live lives of integrity and virtue. The covenant path that will return us to our beloved Father in Heaven and His Son, Jesus Christ, is not obscure; it is well marked. We have been repeatedly taught the principles and covenants essential for this sacred path.

speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Integrity and Virtue Lead to Happiness
quote: The virtuous, Christlike life necessary to sustain us and propel us along the covenant path has never been more important or challenging. If we are to be spiritually prepared to have the integrity and virtue required of disciples of Jesus Christ, we can stay on the path and continue to follow wise, righteous principles that lead to happiness.

speaker: Elder Alfred Kyungu
title: Using the Language of Peacemakers
quote: Let us repent for the harsh language and expressions that have offended our friends, leaders, family members, or colleagues. Let us pray for peaceful communication among us, regardless of the difference in our opinions. Let us use the language that uplifts, edifies, comforts, and brings people together. Let us speak with “warm respect when we speak with each other.” “Let us qualify for His blessings by using the language … of peacemakers.”

speaker: Elder Alfred Kyungu
title: Using the Language of Peacemakers
quote: I began pondering on President Oaks’s invitation and how I could act with faith accordingly. It is a spiritual exercise to identify the language and expressions we need to forgo and then replace them with words and phrases that bring peace wherever we are and at all times.

speaker: Elder Ciro Schmeil
title: Consider Your Ways, and from This Day Will the Lord Bless You
quote: In Preach My Gospel we also learn that “as we make our Sabbath activities compatible with God’s intent for the day, we will feel joy and peace. We will be spiritually nourished and physically refreshed.” What a blessing it is for us to partake of the sacrament each week.

speaker: Elder Ciro Schmeil
title: Consider Your Ways, and from This Day Will the Lord Bless You
quote: We show our faith in Christ by making and keeping covenants with God. “A covenant is a sacred promise between God and His children. God gives the conditions for the covenant, and His children agree to obey those conditions. God promises to bless His children as they fulfill the covenant.”

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All
quote: Along the way we should work to draw closer to Jesus Christ by increasing our humility. President Spencer W. Kimball defined humility as “teachableness.” He explained: “Teachableness [is] an ability to realize that all virtues and abilities are not concentrated in one’s self. … [Humility] is forgiving others in the realization that there may be errors of the same kind or worse [that we ourselves commit].”

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All
quote: Latter-day Saints invite each other and all men and women everywhere to “come unto Christ.” As a prophet has told us in the Book of Mormon, “I would that ye should come unto Christ, who is the Holy One of Israel, and partake of his salvation, and the power of his redemption.”

speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Christ-Centered Unity
quote: Spiritual growth is rarely dramatic at the beginning. Like an exponential curve, it often starts gradually—with loving parents, simple prayers, and small acts of faith.

speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Christ-Centered Unity
quote: When I read the scriptures, I’m impressed with how much of the Savior’s work has to do with bringing people peacefully together. For example, think about the world Jesus Christ was born in. At that time and place, Jews and Samaritans avoided each other. Gentiles were considered unclean. Pharisees and Sadducees agreed on little except their dislike of publicans and sinners. The people were divided in a dozen different ways—culturally, politically, religiously.

speaker: Sister Andrea Muñoz Spannaus
role: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: God Is at Your Side
quote: Our Father and our Savior know you and have the same perfect love for you. Part of that love and mercy is giving us many opportunities and being patient as we learn and work on our list of aspirations.

speaker: Sister Andrea Muñoz Spannaus
role: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: God Is at Your Side
quote: Partake of the sacrament with a humble heart, grateful for the promise that as you keep your covenants, the Holy Ghost will be your constant companion. Begin each day by asking the Father for that companionship.

speaker: Elder Moisés Villanueva
title: “Prove Me Now Herewith”
quote: “And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated” (Doctrine and Covenants 130:20–21).

speaker: Elder Moisés Villanueva
title: “Prove Me Now Herewith”
quote: After a sacrament meeting, a faithful sister shared that her testimony of the law of tithing had begun to weaken. She explained that although she had always paid a full tithe, she had never received the job promotion she had hoped for nor even the salary increase she deserved.

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise
quote: The covenants and ordinances of the Savior’s restored gospel are spiritual credentials that can open wide the heavenly windows of opportunity to receive in our lives divine purpose, direction, and strength. God promises His sons and daughters supernal blessings for honoring covenants, including obedience to the laws and ordinances of the gospel of Jesus Christ. Ongoing faithfulness is required for those credentials to be valid and for promised blessings to be received.

speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise
quote: The sealing of a man and a woman in the house of the Lord is a crowning covenant and ordinance of the Savior’s restored gospel. And importantly, understanding the doctrinal importance of a sealing ordinance being sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise helps to address, in part, deeply personal questions about whether another person’s choices can deprive a faithful covenant keeper of eternal blessings.

speaker: Elder Thabo Lebethoa
title: Jesus Christ Is the Light and Life of the World
quote: Having faith in Jesus Christ means trusting that He understands our daily difficulties and knows how to help us rise above them because He has experienced all our pains, afflictions, and infirmities (see Alma 7:11–12). We need to trust that He is always ready to help us as we remember to “look unto [Him] in every thought” and “doubt not, fear not” (Doctrine and Covenants 6:36).

speaker: Elder Thabo Lebethoa
