title: Jesus Christ Is the Light and Life of the World
quote: In Preach My Gospel, we learn, “As people read and pray about the Book of Mormon, they will come to know the Savior better and experience His love” (Preach My Gospel: A Guide to Sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ [2023], 115).

speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
title: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quote: Well, James cleverly devised a purpose for both. I anxiously watched as James delightedly buttoned his right sleeve to his left jacket lapel. Being pleased with himself quickly gave way to being panicked, because once James had buttoned his arm to his chest, even with the flexibility of a Primary child, he could not get himself loose. James had unintentionally, but quite successfully, created a one-arm straitjacket.

speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
title: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quote: Christlike help encourages spiritually confident discipleship. After receiving help from Jesus Christ, Peter had the confidence to leave behind his large catch of fish to follow Him (see Luke 5:11). Similarly, after experiencing the Savior’s help, the woman at the well had the confidence to leave behind her waterpot to tell everyone of the Messiah (see John 4:28).

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Fruit to Make One Happy
quote: The tree stands for the love of God, including the greatest manifestations of that love: the birth, life, and atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ. The fruit symbolizes blessings received through the Atonement of Jesus Christ, including ordinances, covenants, and truths of the restored gospel and ultimately eternal life.

speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Fruit to Make One Happy
quote: To my young friends, you have been exceptionally good listeners as I illustrated three delicious fruits of the gospel: we are children of a loving Heavenly Father, the great plan of happiness through Jesus Christ, and the gift of the Holy Ghost.

speaker: Brother Gabriel W. Reid
role: Second Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency
title: You Are Good Enough to Teach
quote: Later, after teaching many other precious truths, Jesus invited the people to return home and ponder what they had learned. We may say that “class” had ended, but His love for the people had not. When He perceived the desire of their hearts, He was filled with compassion. He healed their sick, blessed their children, and prayed for them one by one.

speaker: Brother Gabriel W. Reid
role: Second Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency
title: You Are Good Enough to Teach
quote: When asked which commandment was the greatest, the Savior taught, first, to love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul, and mind and, second, to love our neighbor as ourselves.

speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Teach Truth with Love
quote: The fifth principle then is to stay anchored in Jesus Christ. Ask yourself if you carry these Christlike attributes when you are striving to stand for truth with love: “And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in … truth.”

speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Teach Truth with Love
quote: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together. I believe teaching truth with love will be the hallmark of Christ’s disciples in the last days. For some this will require greater conviction. For others it will demand greater charity. I know the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
role: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
title: Closing Remarks
quote: My dear brothers and sisters, the great messages of this conference and the Spirit of the Lord have inspired all of us to concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies on the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan for our eternal increase and joy.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 1 (on “They did eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.”)
quote: Celestial spirits enjoy communion with their Lord, and this is not denied to us; they rest in his love, and we have perfect peace in him: they hymn his praise, and it is our privilege to bless him too.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 3 (on “I will give thee for a covenant of the people.”)
quote: Jesus Christ is himself the sum and substance of the covenant, and as one of its gifts. He is the property of every believer. Believer, canst thou estimate what thou hast gotten in Christ?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 5 (on “And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.”)
quote: Spiritual light has many beams and prismatic colours, but whether they be knowledge, joy, holiness, or life, all are divinely good. If the light received be thus good, what must the essential light be, and how glorious must be the place where he reveals himself.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 7 (on “For me to live is Christ.”)
quote: The believer did not always live to Christ. He began to do so when God the Holy Spirit convinced him of sin, and when by grace he was brought to see the dying Saviour making a propitiation for his guilt.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 9 (on “I will be their God.”)
quote: Dost thou want anything but God? Is not his all-sufficiency enough to satisfy thee if all else should fail? But thou wantest more than quiet satisfaction; thou desirest rapturous delight.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 11 (on “These have no root.”)
quote: If my mind remains as obdurate as it was by nature, the sun of trial will scorch, and my hard heart will help to cast the heat the more terribly upon the ill-covered seed, and my religion will soon die, and my despair will be terrible; therefore, O heavenly Sower, plough me first, and then cast the truth into me, and let me yield thee a bounteous harvest.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 13 (on “Jehoshaphat made ships of Tharshish to go to Ophir for gold: but they went not; for the ships were broken at Ezion-geber”)
quote: Solomon’s ships had returned in safety, but Jehoshaphat’s vessels never reached the land of gold. Providence prospers one, and frustrates the desires of another, in the same business and at the same spot, yet the Great Ruler is as good and wise at one time as another.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 15 (on “Do as thou hast said.”)
quote: Nothing pleases our Lord better than to see his promises put in circulation; he loves to see his children bring them up to him, and say, “Lord, do as thou hast said.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 17 (on “And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion.”)
quote: Through thy tears thine eyes have seen the Lamb of God taking away thy sins. Rejoice, then. In a little while, when thine eyes shall have been wiped from tears, thou wilt see the same Lamb exalted on his throne.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 19 (on “I sought him, but I found him not.”)
quote: Tell me where you lost the company of Christ, and I will tell you the most likely place to find him. Have you lost Christ in the closet by restraining prayer?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 21 (on “And so all Israel shall be saved.”)
quote: When Moses sang at the Red Sea, it was his joy to know that all Israel were safe. Not a drop of spray fell from that solid wall until the last of God’s Israel had safely planted his foot on the other side the flood.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 23 (on “I have exalted one chosen out of the people.”)
quote: Why was Christ chosen out of the people? Speak, my heart, for heart-thoughts are best. Was it not that he might be able to be our brother, in the blest tie of kindred blood?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 25 (on “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us.”)
quote: Or if the love of thine espousals be forgotten, there must surely be some precious milestone along the road of life not quite grown over with moss, on which thou canst read a happy memorial of his mercy towards thee?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 27 (on “And of his fulness have all we received.”)
quote: Come, believer, and get all thy need supplied; ask largely, and thou shalt receive largely, for this “fulness” is inexhaustible, and is treasured up where all the needy may reach it, even in Jesus, Immanuel—God with us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 29 (on “The things which are not seen.”)
quote: Looking into the future we see sin cast out, the body of sin and death destroyed, the soul made perfect, and fit to be a partaker of the inheritance of the saints in light.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, January 31 (on “The Lord our Righteousness.”)
quote: What though distresses afflict me, though Satan assault me, though there may be many things to be experienced before I get to heaven, those are done for me in the covenant of divine grace; there is nothing wanting in my Lord, Christ hath done it all.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 1 (on “They shall sing in the ways of the Lord.”)
quote: The time when Christians begin to sing in the ways of the Lord is when they first lose their burden at the foot of the Cross. Not even the songs of the angels seem so sweet as the first song of rapture which gushes from the inmost soul of the forgiven child of God.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 3 (on “Therefore, brethren, we are debtors.”)
quote: What a debtor thou art to divine sovereignty! How much thou owest to his disinterested love, for he gave his own Son that he might die for thee.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 5 (on “The Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.”)
quote: Didst thou ever consider the depth of love in the heart of Jehovah, when God the Father equipped his Son for the great enterprise of mercy? If not, be this thy day’s meditation.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 7 (on “Arise, and depart.”)
quote: We shall be departing from all we have known and loved here, but we shall be going to our Father’s house—to our Father’s home, where Jesus is—to that royal “city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 9 (on “And David enquired of the Lord.”)
quote: Many a rock might be escaped, if we would let our Father take the helm; many a shoal or quicksand we might well avoid, if we would leave to his sovereign will to choose and to command.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 11 (on “And they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.”)
quote: Imitate him in your loving spirit; think kindly, speak kindly, and do kindly, that men may say of you, “He has been with Jesus.” Imitate Jesus in his holiness.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 13 (on “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God.”)
quote: Does your faith almost fail you? Fear not, it is neither your graces nor feelings on which you are to live: you must live simply by faith on Christ.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 15 (on “To him be glory both now and forever.”)
quote: O Jesus! thou shalt be praised forever. Long as immortal spirits live—long as the Father’s throne endures—forever, forever, unto thee shall be glory. Believer, you are anticipating the time when you shall join the saints above in ascribing all glory to Jesus; but are you glorifying him now?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 17 (on “Isaac dwelt by the well Lahai-roi.”)
quote: Let us learn to live in the presence of the living God; let us pray the Holy Spirit that this day, and every other day, we may feel, “Thou God seest me.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 19 (on “Thus saith the Lord God; I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them.”)
quote: Or, to use another illustration, when God piles up a hill of mercies, he himself shines behind them, and he casts on our spirits the shadow of prayer, so that we may rest certain, if we are much in prayer, our pleadings are the shadows of mercy.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 21 (on “He hath said.”)
quote: Yes; whether for delight in our quietude, or for strength in our conflict, “He hath said” must be our daily resort. And this may teach us the extreme value of searching the Scriptures.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 23 (on “I will never leave thee.”)
quote: Lift up now thine eyes to the north and to the south, to the east and to the west, for all this is thine. Climb to Pisgah’s top, and view the utmost limit of the divine promise, for the land is all thine own.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 25 (on “The wrath to come.”)
quote: Where, where, where, O sinner, wilt thou hide thy head, or whither wilt thou flee? O that the hand of mercy may now lead you to Christ! He is freely set before you in the gospel: his riven side is the rock of shelter.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, February 27 (on “Thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation.”)
quote: “Yet,” says Moses, “though we are always changing, Lord, thou hast been our dwelling-place throughout all generations.” The Christian knows no change with regard to God. He may be rich today and poor to-morrow; he may be sickly today and well to-morrow; he may be in happiness today, to-morrow he may be distressed—but there is no change with regard to his relationship to God.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 1 (on “Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out.”)
quote: Anything is better than the dead calm of indifference. Our souls may wisely desire the north wind of trouble if that alone can be sanctified to the drawing forth of the perfume of our graces.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 3 (on “I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.”)
quote: If, believer, thou requirest still greater comfort, remember that you have the Son of Man with you in the furnace. In that silent chamber of yours, there sitteth by your side One whom thou hast not seen, but whom thou lovest; and ofttimes when thou knowest it not, he makes all thy bed in thy affliction, and smooths thy pillow for thee.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 5 (on “Let us not sleep, as do others.”)
quote: Christians who isolate themselves and walk alone, are very liable to grow drowsy. Hold Christian company, and you will be kept wakeful by it, and refreshed and encouraged to make quicker progress in the road to heaven.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 7 (on “Have faith in God.”)
quote: Would you be comfortable and happy? Would you enjoy religion? Would you have the religion of cheerfulness and not that of gloom? Then “have faith in God.” If you love darkness, and are satisfied to dwell in gloom and misery, then be content with little faith; but if you love the sunshine, and would sing songs of rejoicing, covet earnestly this best gift, “great faith.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 9 (on “Yea, he is altogether lovely.”)
quote: The superlative beauty of Jesus is all-attracting; it is not so much to be admired as to be loved. He is more than pleasant and fair, he is lovely.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 11 (on “Sin ... exceeding sinful.”)
quote: Beware of light thoughts of sin. At the time of conversion, the conscience is so tender, that we are afraid of the slightest sin. Young converts have a holy timidity, a godly fear lest they should offend against God.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 13 (on “Why sit we here until we die?”)
quote: None escape who refuse to look to Jesus; but you know that, at any rate, some are saved who believe in him, for certain of your own acquaintances have received mercy: then why not you?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 15 (on “Be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.”)
quote: Let us make daily use of our riches, and ever repair to him as to our own Lord in covenant, taking from him the supply of all we need with as much boldness as men take money from their own purse.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 17 (on “Remember the poor.”)
quote: We show our love to Christ when we sing of him and when we pray to him; but if there were no sons of need in the world we should lose the sweet privilege of evidencing our love, by ministering in alms-giving to his poorer brethren; he has ordained that thus we should prove that our love standeth not in word only, but in deed and in truth.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 19 (on “Strong in faith.”)
quote: Christian, take good care of thy faith; for recollect faith is the only way whereby thou canst obtain blessings. If we want blessings from God, nothing can fetch them down but faith.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 21 (on “Ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone.”)
quote: Occupied with the passover feast at their own houses, they represent the many who live upon the letter, but are mere babes as to the spirit of the gospel.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 23 (on “His sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.”)
quote: The cheeks are pale; a fainting fit comes on; the blood has gone inward as if to nourish the inner man while passing through its trial. But see our Saviour in his agony; he is so utterly oblivious of self, that instead of his agony driving his blood to the heart to nourish himself, it drives it outward to bedew the earth.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 25 (on “Betrayest thou the Son of Man with a kiss?”)
quote: “The kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Let me be on my guard when the world puts on a loving face, for it will, if possible, betray me as it did my Master, with a kiss.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 27 (on “Then all the disciples forsook him and fled.”)
quote: Divine grace can make the coward brave. The smoking flax can flame forth like fire on the altar when the Lord wills it. These very apostles who were timid as hares, grew to be bold as lions after the Spirit had descended upon them, and even so the Holy Spirit can make my recreant spirit brave to confess my Lord and witness for his truth.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 29 (on “Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered.”)
quote: “He is not an high priest that cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities.” In this sympathy of Christ we find a sustaining power. One of the early martyrs said, “I can bear it all, for Jesus suffered, and he suffers in me now; he sympathizes with me, and this makes me strong.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, March 31 (on “With his stripes we are healed.”)
quote: Believer in Jesus, can you gaze upon him without tears, as he stands before you the mirror of agonizing love? He is at once fair as the lily for innocence, and red as the rose with the crimson of his own blood.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 1 (on “Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.”)
quote: Faith is our walk, but fellowship sensibly felt is our rest. Faith is the road, but communion with Jesus is the well from which the pilgrim drinks. O lover of our souls, be not strange to us; let the lips of thy blessing meet the lips of our asking; let the lips of thy fulness touch the lips of our need, and straightway the kiss will be effected.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 3 (on “They took Jesus, and led him away.”)
quote: What learn we here as we see our blessed Lord led forth? Do we not perceive that truth which was set forth in shadow by the scapegoat? Did not the high-priest bring the scapegoat, and put both his hands upon its head, confessing the sins of the people, that thus those sins might be laid upon the goat, and cease from the people?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 5 (on “On him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.”)
quote: Surely we should love the cross, and, instead of shrinking from it, count it very dear, when it works out for us “a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 9 (on “And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.”)
quote: Out of Magdalene seven devils were cast—but a whole legion out of me. Mary and Martha were favoured with visits—but he dwells with me. His mother bare his body—but he is formed in me the hope of glory.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 11 (on “I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint.”)
quote: Did earth or heaven ever behold a sadder spectacle of woe! In soul and body, our Lord felt himself to be weak as water poured upon the ground.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 13 (on “A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me.”)
quote: We must value him as our best treasure; we must prize his words and his ordinances; and we must keep our thoughts of him and knowledge of him as under lock and key, lest the devil should steal anything from us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 15 (on “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?”)
quote: Some of us think at times that we could cry, “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” There are seasons when the brightness of our Father’s smile is eclipsed by clouds and darkness; but let us remember that God never does really forsake us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 17 (on “Ye are come to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.”)
quote: Reader, have you come to the blood of sprinkling? The question is not whether you have come to a knowledge of doctrine, or an observance of ceremonies, or to a certain form of experience, but have you come to the blood of Jesus?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 19 (on “Behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.”)
quote: Life and immortality are now brought to light, and things which have been hidden since the foundation of the world are manifest in him. The annual ceremony of atonement was thus abolished.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 21 (on “I know that my Redeemer liveth.”)
quote: Rest not content until by faith you can say “Yes, I cast myself upon my living Lord; and he is mine.” It may be you hold him with a feeble hand; you half think it presumption to say, “He lives as my Redeemer;” yet, remember if you have but faith as a grain of mustard seed, that little faith entitles you to say it.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 23 (on “Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.”)
quote: Ordinances are nothing without Christ as a means of mortification. Your prayers, and your repentances, and your tears—the whole of them put together—are worth nothing apart from him.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 25 (on “Rise up my love, my fair one, and come away.”)
quote: Lo, I hear the voice of my Beloved! He speaks to me! Fair weather is smiling upon the face of the earth, and he would not have me spiritually asleep while nature is all around me awaking from her winter’s rest.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 27 (on “God, even our own God.”)
quote: Fly to him, tell him all thy wants. Use him constantly by faith at all times. If some dark providence has beclouded thee, use thy God as a “sun;” if some strong enemy has beset thee, find in Jehovah a “shield,” for he is a sun and shield to his people.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, April 29 (on “Thou art my hope in the day of evil.”)
quote: Oh! say not so, thou who art walking in darkness. The best of God’s saints must drink the wormwood; the dearest of his children must bear the cross.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 1 (on “His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers.”)
quote: Thou didst not hide thy face from shame and spitting, O Lord Jesus, and therefore I will find my dearest delight in praising thee. Those cheeks were furrowed by the plough of grief, and crimsoned with red lines of blood from thy thorn-crowned temples; such marks of love unbounded cannot but charm my soul far more than “pillars of perfume.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 3 (on “In the world ye shall have tribulation.”)
quote: Wilt thou easily be conformed to his image? Wilt thou not require much refining in the furnace of affliction to purify thee? Will it be an easy thing to get rid of thy corruptions, and make thee perfect even as thy Father which is in heaven is perfect?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 5 (on “I will be their God, and they shall be my people.”)
quote: Canst thou read the Book of Inspiration, and find there the indentures of thy salvation? Canst thou read thy title writ in precious blood? Canst thou, by humble faith, lay hold of Jesus’ garments, and say, “My Christ”?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 7 (on “Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all.”)
quote: Whatever my own case may be, the beloved Physician can heal me; and whatever may be the state of others whom I may remember at this moment in prayer, I may have hope in Jesus that he will be able to heal them of their sins.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 9 (on “Who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings.”)
quote: The eternal covenant, based upon suretiship and confirmed by oath, is ours, for our strong consolation and security. In the everlasting settlements of predestinating wisdom and omnipotent decree, the eye of the Lord Jesus was ever fixed on us; and we may rest assured that in the whole roll of destiny there is not a line which militates against the interests of his redeemed.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 11 (on “I am with you alway.”)
quote: My soul, I charge thee, lay up thy treasure in the only secure cabinet; store thy jewels where thou canst never lose them. Put thine all in Christ; set all thine affections on his person, all thy hope in his merit, all thy trust in his efficacious blood, all thy joy in his presence, and so thou mayest laugh at loss, and defy destruction.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 13 (on “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.”)
quote: Be patient! The Husbandman waits until he reaps his harvest. Be patient; for you know who has said, “Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give to every man according as his work shall be.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 15 (on “All that believe are justified.”)
quote: The thief upon the cross was justified the moment that he turned the eye of faith to Jesus; and Paul, the aged, after years of service, was not more justified than was the thief with no service at all.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 17 (on “So to walk even as he walked.”)
quote: For their own happiness’ sake, if they would drink wine on the lees, well refined; if they would enjoy holy and happy communion with Jesus; if they would be lifted up above the cares and troubles of this world, let them walk even as he walked.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 19 (on “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.”)
quote: The Holy Spirit loves order, and he therefore sets our powers and faculties in due rank and place, giving the highest room to those spiritual faculties which link us with the great King; let us not disturb the divine arrangement, but ask for grace that we may keep under our body and bring it into subjection.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 21 (on “If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.”)
quote: Do not rest, O believer, till thou hast a full assurance of thine interest in Jesus. Let nothing satisfy thee till, by the infallible witness of the Holy Spirit bearing witness with thy spirit, thou art certified that thou art a child of God.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 23 (on “The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me.”)
quote: Most manifestly the confidence which the Psalmist here expressed was a divine confidence. He did not say, “I have grace enough to perfect that which concerneth me—my faith is so steady that it will not stagger—my love is so warm that it will never grow cold—my resolution is so firm that nothing can move it”; no, his dependence was on the Lord alone.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 25 (on “Forsake me not, O Lord.”)
quote: Forsake me not in my joys, lest they absorb my heart. Forsake me not in my sorrows, lest I murmur against thee. Forsake me not in the day of my repentance, lest I lose the hope of pardon, and fall into despair; and forsake me not in the day of my strongest faith, lest faith degenerate into presumption.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 27 (on “So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.”)
quote: The Lord’s people are dear for another’s sake. Such is the love which the Father bears to his only begotten, that for his sake he raises his lowly brethren from poverty and banishment, to courtly companionship, noble rank, and royal provision.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 29 (on “Thou hatest wickedness.”)
quote: “Be ye angry, and sin not.” There can hardly be goodness in a man if he be not angry at sin; he who loves truth must hate every false way.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, May 31 (on “The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron.”)
quote: God had one Son without sin, but not a single child without the rod. It is a great joy to believe that Jesus has been tempted in all points like as we are.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 1 (on “The evening and the morning were the first day.”)
quote: Study next, to make the outgoings of the morning and the evening to rejoice. Praise the Lord for the sun of joy when it rises, and for the gloom of evening as it falls.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 3 (on “These were potters, and those that dwelt among plants and hedges: there they dwelt with the king for his work.”)
quote: The place of our habitation is fixed, and we are not to remove from it out of whim and caprice, but seek to serve the Lord in it, by being a blessing to those among whom we reside.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 5 (on “The Lord shut him in.”)
quote: We are not of the world even as our Lord Jesus was not of the world. Into the sin, the gaiety, the pursuits of the multitude we cannot enter; we cannot play in the streets of Vanity Fair with the children of darkness, for our heavenly Father has shut us in.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 7 (on “Ye that love the Lord hate evil.”)
quote: We have good reason, indeed, for hating evil when we look back and trace its deadly workings. Such mischief did evil do us, that our souls would have been lost had not omnipotent love interfered to redeem us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 9 (on “The Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad.”)
quote: The deeper our troubles, the louder our thanks to God, who has led us through all, and preserved us until now. Our griefs cannot mar the melody of our praise, we reckon them to be the bass part of our life’s song, “He hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 11 (on “We love him because he first loved us.”)
quote: Our love to him is the fair offspring of his love to us. Cold admiration, when studying the works of God, anyone may have, but the warmth of love can only be kindled in the heart by God’s Spirit.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 13 (on “Whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.”)
quote: You have no belief and no repentance,—come to him, and he will give them to you. Come just as you are, and take “Freely,” without money and without price.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 15 (on “And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.”)
quote: The Lord Jesus is a deep sea of joy: my soul shall dive therein, shall be swallowed up in the delights of his society. Sarah looked on her Isaac, and laughed with excess of rapture, and all her friends laughed with her; and thou, my soul, look on thy Jesus, and bid heaven and earth unite in thy joy unspeakable.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 17 (on “Help, Lord.”)
quote: The occasions for the use of this prayer are frequent. In providential afflictions how suitable it is for tried believers who find all helpers failing them. Students, in doctrinal difficulties, may often obtain aid by lifting up this cry of “Help, Lord,” to the Holy Spirit, the great Teacher.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 19 (on “And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.”)
quote: Life, comfort, light, purity, power, peace; and many other precious blessings are inseparable from the Spirit’s benign presence. As sacred oil, he anoints the head of the believer, sets him apart to the priesthood of saints, and gives him grace to execute his office aright.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 21 (on “Thou art fairer than the children of men.”)
quote: Oh, Jesus! thy power, thy grace, thy justice, thy tenderness, thy truth, thy majesty, and thine immutability make up such a man, or rather such a God-man, as neither heaven nor earth hath seen elsewhere.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 23 (on “Ephraim is a cake not turned.”)
quote: To be sanctified, spirit, soul, and body, should be thine aim and prayer; and although sanctification may not be perfect in thee anywhere in degree, yet it must be universal in its action; there must not be the appearance of holiness in one place and reigning sin in another, else thou, too, wilt be a cake not turned.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 25 (on “Get thee up into the high mountain.”)
quote: Our knowledge of Christ is somewhat like climbing one of our Welsh mountains. When you are at the base you see but little: the mountain itself appears to be but one-half as high as it really is.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 27 (on “Only ye shall not go very far away.”)
quote: Worldly wisdom recommends the path of compromise, and talks of “moderation.” According to this carnal policy, purity is admitted to be very desirable, but we are warned against being too precise; truth is of course to be followed, but error is not to be severely denounced.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, June 29 (on “Them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.”)
quote: The toil-worn believer quietly sleeps, as does the weary child when it slumbers on its mother’s breast. Oh! happy they who die in the Lord; they rest from their labours, and their works do follow them.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 1 (on “In summer and in winter shall it be.”)
quote: By turning the course of the Euphrates, Cyrus took the city of Babylon, but no power, human or infernal, can divert the current of divine grace. The tracks of ancient rivers have been found all dry and desolate, but the streams which take their rise on the mountains of divine sovereignty and infinite love shall ever be full to the brim.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 3 (on “The ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven wellfavoured and fat kine.”)
quote: Why should not every year be richer than the past, in love, and usefulness, and joy?—I am nearer the celestial hills, I have had more experience of my Lord, and should be more like Him.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 5 (on “Called to be saints.”)
quote: We are very apt to regard the apostolic saints as if they were “saints” in a more especial manner than the other children of God. All are “saints” whom God has called by His grace, and sanctified by His Spirit; but we are apt to look upon the apostles as extraordinary beings, scarcely subject to the same weaknesses and temptations as ourselves.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 7 (on “Brethren, pray for us.”)
quote: Our sacred calling involves us in temptations from which you are exempt, above all it too often draws us away from our personal enjoyment of truth into a ministerial and official consideration of it.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 9 (on “Forget not all His benefits.”)
quote: Let our souls give forth music as sweet and as exhilarating as came from David’s harp, while we praise the Lord whose mercy endureth forever.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 11 (on “After that ye have suffered awhile, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.”)
quote: A glorious show made up of transitory sun-beams and passing rain-drops, how can it abide? The graces of the Christian character must not resemble the rainbow in its transitory beauty, but, on the contrary, must be stablished, settled, abiding.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 13 (on “God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry?”)
quote: We must not make natural infirmity an excuse for sin, but we must fly to the cross and pray the Lord to crucify our tempers, and renew us in gentleness and meekness after His own image.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 15 (on “The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out.”)
quote: Keep the altar of private prayer burning. This is the very life of all piety. The sanctuary and family altars borrow their fires here, therefore let this burn well.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 17 (on “Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God.”)
quote: Christ was at the everlasting council: he can tell you whether you were chosen or not; but you cannot find it out in any other way. Go and put your trust in him, and his answer will be—“I have loved thee with an everlasting love, therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 19 (on “The Lord our God hath shewed us his glory.”)
quote: Among the huge Atlantic-waves of bereavement, poverty, temptation, and reproach, we learn the power of Jehovah, because we feel the littleness of man. Thank God, then, if you have been led by a rough road: it is this which has given you your experience of God’s greatness and lovingkindness.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 21 (on “The daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.”)
quote: Reassured by the Word of the Lord, the poor trembling citizens of Zion grew bold, and shook their heads at Sennacherib’s boastful threats. Strong faith enables the servants of God to look with calm contempt upon their most haughty foes.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 23 (on “Even thou wast as one of them.”)
quote: Brotherly kindness was due from Edom to Israel in the time of need, but instead thereof, the men of Esau made common cause with Israel’s foes. Special stress in the sentence before us is laid upon the word thou; as when Caesar cried to Brutus, “and thou Brutus”; a bad action may be all the worse, because of the person who has committed it.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 25 (on “He left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.”)
quote: No ties of friendship, no chains of beauty, no flashings of talent, no shafts of ridicule must turn me from the wise resolve to flee from sin. The devil I am to resist and he will flee from me, but the lusts of the flesh, I must flee, or they will surely overcome me.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 27 (on “Exceeding great and precious promises.”)
quote: If you would know experimentally the preciousness of the promises, and enjoy them in your own heart, meditate much upon them. There are promises which are like grapes in the wine-press; if you will tread them the juice will flow.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 29 (on “Nevertheless I am continually with thee.”)
quote: Believer, you are forced to enter into Asaph’s confession and acknowledgment, endeavour in like spirit to say “nevertheless, since I belong to Christ I am continually with God!”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, July 31 (on “I in them.”)
quote: Why, believer, dost not thou sit at his banquet of wine? Seek thy Lord, for he is near; embrace him, for he is thy Brother. Hold Him fast, for he is thine Husband; and press him to thine heart, for he is of thine own flesh.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 1 (on “Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn.”)
quote: Wilt thou not obey him, and come to him even now? Take another ear of corn: “Fear not, thou worm Jacob, I will help thee, saith the Lord and thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 3 (on “The Lamb is the light thereof.”)
quote: Quietly contemplate the Lamb as the light of heaven. Light in Scripture is the emblem of joy. The joy of the saints in heaven is comprised in this: Jesus chose us, loved us, bought us, cleansed us, robed us, kept us, glorified us: we are here entirely through the Lord Jesus.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 5 (on “We know that all things work together for good to them that love God.”)
quote: Every event as yet has worked out the most divinely blessed results; and so, believing that God rules all, that he governs wisely, that he brings good out of evil, the believer’s heart is assured, and he is enabled calmly to meet each trial as it comes.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 7 (on “The upright love thee”)
quote: Believers love Jesus with a deeper affection than they dare to give to any other being. They would sooner lose father and mother than part with Christ. They hold all earthly comforts with a loose hand, but they carry him fast locked in their bosoms.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 9 (on “The city hath no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it.”)
quote: Oh! what a blessed time shall that be when we shall have mounted above every second cause and shall rest upon the bare arm of God! What a glorious hour when God, and not his creatures; the Lord, and not his works, shall be our daily joy!

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 11 (on “Oh that I were as in months past.”)
quote: Christian, if you are not now as you “were in months past,” do not rest satisfied with wishing for a return of former happiness, but go at once to seek your Master, and tell him your sad state.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 13 (on “The cedars of Lebanon which he hath planted.”)
quote: Lebanon’s cedars are emblematic of the Christian, in that they owe their planting entirely to the Lord. This is quite true of every child of God. He is not man-planted, nor self-planted, but God-planted.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 15 (on “Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide.”)
quote: When Jesus is the theme, meditation is sweet indeed. Isaac found Rebecca while engaged in private musings; many others have found their best beloved there.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 19 (on “He shall stand and feed in the strength of the Lord.”)
quote: Happy are we who belong to such a shepherd, whose humanity communes with us, and whose divinity protects us. Let us worship and bow down before him as the people of his pasture.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 21 (on “He that watereth shall be watered also himself.”)
quote: We are here taught the great lesson, that to get, we must give; that to accumulate, we must scatter; that to make ourselves happy, we must make others happy; and that in order to become spiritually vigorous, we must seek the spiritual good of others.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 23 (on “The voice of weeping shall be no more heard.”)
quote: The joy of Christ, which is an infinite fulness of delight, is in them. They bathe themselves in the bottomless, shoreless sea of infinite beatitude. That same joyful rest remains for us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 25 (on “His fruit was sweet to my taste.”)
quote: Faith, in the Scripture, is spoken of under the emblem of all the senses. It is sight: “Look unto me and be ye saved.” It is hearing: “Hear, and your soul shall live.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 27 (on “How long will it be ere they believe me?”)
quote: Strive with all diligence to keep out that monster unbelief. It so dishonours Christ, that he will withdraw his visible presence if we insult him by indulging it.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 29 (on “Have mercy upon me, O God.”)
quote: If mercy be needed to be exercised towards our duties, what shall be said of our sins? How sweet the remembrance that inexhaustible mercy is waiting to be gracious to us, to restore our backslidings, and make our broken bones rejoice!

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, August 31 (on “On mine arm shall they trust.”)
quote: Now is the time for feats of faith and valiant exploits. Be strong and very courageous, and the Lord thy God shall certainly, as surely as he built the heavens and the earth, glorify himself in thy weakness, and magnify his might in the midst of thy distress.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 1 (on “Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.”)
quote: A sense of our own folly is a great step towards being wise, when it leads us to rely on the wisdom of the Lord. The blind man leans on his friend’s arm and reaches home in safety, and so would we give ourselves up implicitly to divine guidance, nothing doubting; assured that though we cannot see, it is always safe to trust the all-seeing God.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 3 (on “Thou whom my soul loveth.”)
quote: No one ought to give any rest to his spirit till he feels quite sure about a matter of such vital importance. We ought not to be satisfied with a superficial hope that Jesus loves us, and with a bare trust that we love him.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 7 (on “And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.”)
quote: All means are good and decorous when faith and love are truly set on winning souls. If hunger for bread can break through stone walls, surely hunger for souls is not to be hindered in its efforts.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 9 (on “I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things which thou knowest not.”)
quote: Prevailing prayer takes the Christian to Carmel, and enables him to cover heaven with clouds of blessing, and earth with floods of mercy. Prevailing prayer bears the Christian aloft to Pisgah, and shows him the inheritance reserved; it elevates us to Tabor and transfigures us, till in the likeness of his Lord, as he is, so are we also in this world.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 11 (on “Be ye separate.”)
quote: You may strive to be rich; but be it your ambition to be “rich in faith,” and good works. You may have pleasure; but when you are merry, sing psalms and make melody in your hearts to the Lord.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 13 (on “Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well, the rain also filleth the pools.”)
quote: May our readers have showers of blessing, and may the wells they have digged be filled with water! Oh, what are means and ordinances without the smile of heaven!

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 15 (on “He shall not be afraid of evil tidings.”)
quote: Trust in the Lord, and wait patiently for him. Your wisest course is to do as Moses did at the Red Sea, “Stand still and see the salvation of God.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 17 (on “Bring him unto me.”)
quote: Despairingly the poor disappointed father turned away from the disciples to their Master. His son was in the worst possible condition, and all means had failed, but the miserable child was soon delivered from the evil one when the parent in faith obeyed the Lord Jesus’ word, “Bring him unto me.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 19 (on “The liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.”)
quote: Come in faith and you are welcome to all covenant blessings. There is not a promise in the Word which shall be withheld. In the depths of tribulations let this freedom comfort you; amidst waves of distress let it cheer you; when sorrows surround thee let it be thy solace.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 21 (on “I will rejoice over them to do them good.”)
quote: Should not we utter our grateful response to such a marvellous declaration of his love, and sing, “I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation?”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 23 (on “Accepted in the beloved.”)
quote: When their spirit is lively, and their hopes bright, they think God accepts them, for they feel so high, so heavenly-minded, so drawn above the earth! But when their souls cleave to the dust, they are the victims of the fear that they are no longer accepted.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 25 (on “Just, and the justifier of him which believeth.”)
quote: My faith rests not upon what I am, or shall be, or feel, or know, but in what Christ is, in what he has done, and in what he is now doing for me.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 27 (on “Happy art thou, O Israel; who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord!”)
quote: The rod of chastisement must rest upon us in our measure, but it worketh for us the comfortable fruits of righteousness; and therefore by the aid of the divine Comforter, we, the “people saved of the Lord,” will joy in the God of our salvation.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, September 29 (on “Behold, if the leprosy have covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague.”)
quote: Nothing is more deadly than self-righteousness, or more hopeful than contrition. We must confess that we are “nothing else but sin,” for no confession short of this will be the whole truth, and if the Holy Spirit be at work with us, convincing us of sin, there will be no difficulty about making such an acknowledgment—it will spring spontaneously from our lips.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 1 (on “Pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.”)
quote: Old sins we must regret, but then we have had repentances which he has given us, by which we have wept our way to the cross, and learned the merit of his blood.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 3 (on “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”)
quote: Angels are the unseen attendants of the saints of God; they bear us up in their hands, lest we dash our foot against a stone. Loyalty to their Lord leads them to take a deep interest in the children of his love; they rejoice over the return of the prodigal to his father’s house below, and they welcome the advent of the believer to the King’s palace above.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 5 (on “He arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights.”)
quote: Some Christians are for living on Christ, but are not so anxious to live for Christ. Earth should be a preparation for heaven; and heaven is the place where saints feast most and work most.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 7 (on “Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant?”)
quote: A faith which can say, in the direst trouble, “Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him,” is heaven-born faith. The Lord afflicts his servants to glorify himself, for he is greatly glorified in the graces of his people, which are his own handiwork.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 9 (on “Able to keep you from falling.”)
quote: Oh, if we are kept from falling, how must we bless the patient power which watches over us day by day! Think, how prone we are to sin, how apt to choose danger, how strong our tendency to cast ourselves down, and these reflections will make us sing more sweetly than we have ever done, “Glory be to him, who is able to keep us from falling.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 11 (on “Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.”)
quote: We thank thee, great God, for the mercy-seat, a choice proof of thy marvellous lovingkindness. Help us to use it aright throughout this day!

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 13 (on “Godly sorrow worketh repentance.”)
quote: Sincere repentance is continual. Believers repent until their dying day. This dropping well is not intermittent. Every other sorrow yields to time, but this dear sorrow grows with our growth, and it is so sweet a bitter, that we thank God we are permitted to enjoy and to suffer it until we enter our eternal rest.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 17 (on “And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul.”)
quote: Ah, no! our God has not left us at any time. We have had dark nights, but the star of love has shone forth amid the blackness; we have been in stern conflicts, but over our head he has held aloft the shield of our defence.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 19 (on “Babes in Christ.”)
quote: Are you mourning, believer, because you are so weak in the divine life: because your faith is so little, your love so feeble? Cheer up, for you have cause for gratitude.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 21 (on “The love of Christ constraineth us.”)
quote: Give not a mere wordy offering to a dying Redeemer. How will you feel when your Master comes, if you have to confess that you did nothing for him, but kept your love shut up, like a stagnant pool, neither flowing forth to his poor or to his work.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 23 (on “Will ye also go away?”)
quote: Have you not up till now found your Lord to be a compassionate and generous friend to you, and has not simple faith in him given you all the peace your spirit could desire?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 25 (on “For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us forever.”)
quote: What a thousand mercies are wrapped up in the assurance that the truth will be with us forever; will be our living support, our dying comfort, our rising song, our eternal glory; this is Christian privilege, without it our faith were little worth.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 27 (on “It is a faithful saying.”)
quote: The last sets forth the active form of Christian service, bidding us diligently to maintain good works. Thus we have the root of salvation in free grace; next, the privileges of that salvation in the life which now is, and in that which is to come; and we have also the two great branches of suffering with Christ and serving with Christ, loaded with the fruits of the Spirit.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 29 (on “After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, etc.”)
quote: The man who is really forgiven, is anxious not to offend again; the possession of justification leads to an anxious desire for sanctification. “Forgive us our debts,” that is justification; “Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil,” that is sanctification in its negative and positive forms.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, October 31 (on “Renew a right spirit within me.”)
quote: Let thy personal weakness, O Christian, be an argument to make thee pray earnestly to thy God for help. Remember, David when he felt himself to be powerless, did not fold his arms or close his lips, but he hastened to the mercy-seat with “renew a right spirit within me.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 1 (on “The church in thy house.”)
quote: How would father’s heart leap for joy, and mother’s eyes fill with holy tears if from the eldest to the youngest all were saved! Let us pray for this great mercy until the Lord shall grant it to us.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 5 (on “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.”)
quote: Let our hearts and lips exclaim, “We have heard with our ears, and our fathers have told us the wondrous things which thou didst in their day, and in the old time before them.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 7 (on “Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands.”)
quote: “Behold,” is a word intended to excite admiration. Here, indeed, we have a theme for marvelling. Heaven and earth may well be astonished that rebels should obtain so great a nearness to the heart of infinite love as to be written upon the palms of his hands.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 9 (on “So walk ye in him.”)
quote: Walking signifies progress. “So walk ye in him”; proceed from grace to grace, run forward until you reach the uttermost degree of knowledge that a man can attain concerning our Beloved.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 11 (on “Underneath are the everlasting arms.”)
quote: Every earthly prop is cut away. What then? Still underneath him are “the everlasting arms.” He cannot fall so deep in distress and affliction but what the covenant grace of an ever-faithful God will still encircle him.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 13 (on “The branch cannot bear fruit of itself.”)
quote: Have you declined since then? If you have, we charge you to remember that time of love, and repent, and do thy first works. Be most in those engagements which you have experimentally proved to draw you nearest to Christ, because it is from him that all your fruits proceed.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 15 (on “The Lord’s portion is his people.”)
quote: Not with corruptible things, as with silver and gold, but with the precious blood of the Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord’s portion has been fully redeemed. There is no mortgage on his estate; no suits can be raised by opposing claimants, the price was paid in open court, and the Church is the Lord’s freehold forever.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 17 (on “To whom be glory forever. Amen”)
quote: Does your knowledge grow? Then sing more sweetly. Do you enjoy happier times than you once had? Have you been restored from sickness, and has your sorrow been turned into peace and joy?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 19 (on “Avoid foolish questions.”)
quote: Our business is neither to ask nor answer foolish questions, but to avoid them altogether; and if we observe the apostle’s precept (Titus 3:8) to be careful to maintain good works, we shall find ourselves far too much occupied with profitable business to take much interest in unworthy, contentious, and needless strivings.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 21 (on “Grieve not the Holy Spirit.”)
quote: Do you desire to speak for Jesus—how can you unless the Holy Ghost touch your tongue? Do you desire to pray? Alas! what dull work it is unless the Spirit maketh intercession for you!

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 23 (on “Fellowship with him.”)
quote: The disciple should not be above his Lord. In our measure we commune with him in his labours, ministering to men by the word of truth and by deeds of love.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 25 (on “To preach deliverance to the captives.”)
quote: Not more free is the eagle which mounts to his rocky eyrie, and afterwards outsoars the clouds, than the soul which Christ hath delivered. If we are no more under the law, but free from its curse, let our liberty be practically exhibited in our serving God with gratitude and delight.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 27 (on “Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord.”)
quote: In Joshua the high priest we see a picture of each and every child of God, who has been made nigh by the blood of Christ, and has been taught to minister in holy things, and enter into that which is within the veil.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, November 29 (on “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people ... Thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”)
quote: Hundreds have been saved from gross sins by the timely, wise, affectionate warnings of faithful ministers and brethren. Our Lord Jesus has set us a gracious example of how to deal with erring friends in his warning given to Peter, the prayer with which he preceded it, and the gentle way in which he bore with Peter’s boastful denial that he needed such a caution.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 1 (on “Thou hast made summer and winter.”)
quote: Let us draw nigh to him, and in him find joy and peace in believing. Let us wrap ourselves in the warm garments of his promises, and go forth to labours which befit the season, for it were ill to be as the sluggard who will not plough by reason of the cold; for he shall beg in summer and have nothing.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 3 (on “There is no spot in thee.”)
quote: A spot may soon be removed, and is the very least thing that can disfigure beauty, but even from this little blemish the believer is delivered in his Lord’s sight.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 5 (on “Ask, and it shall be given you.”)
quote: No bashfulness need retard when Jesus invites. No unbelief should hinder when Jesus promises. No cold-heartedness should restrain when such blessings are to be obtained.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 7 (on “Base things of the world hath God chosen.”)
quote: Redeeming love has set apart many of the worst of mankind to be the reward of the Saviour’s passion. Effectual grace calls forth many of the vilest of the vile to sit at the table of mercy, and therefore let none despair.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 9 (on “Therefore will the Lord wait that he may be gracious unto you.”)
quote: God often delays in answering prayer. We have several instances of this in sacred Scripture. Jacob did not get the blessing from the angel until near the dawn of day—he had to wrestle all night for it.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 11 (on “Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.”)
quote: Believer, let us often reflect with joy on the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints, and honour the faithfulness of our God by a holy confidence in him.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 13 (on “Salt without prescribing how much.”)
quote: More wealth brings more care, but more grace brings more joy. Increased wisdom is increased sorrow, but abundance of the Spirit is fulness of joy. Believer, go to the throne for a large supply of heavenly salt.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 15 (on “Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her.”)
quote: The after gain will be an abundant recompense, for Egypt’s treasures are not to be compared with the glory to be revealed. Orpah is heard of no more; in glorious ease and idolatrous pleasure her life melts into the gloom of death; but Ruth lives in history and in heaven, for grace has placed her in the noble line whence sprung the King of kings.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 17 (on “I remember thee.”)
quote: From all eternity “His delights were with the sons of men;” his thoughts rolled onward to the time when his elect should be born into the world; he viewed them in the mirror of his foreknowledge.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 19 (on “The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.”)
quote: Be wise and attend to the obeying, and let Christ manage the providing. Come and survey your Father’s storehouse, and ask whether he will let you starve while he has laid up so great an abundance in his garner?

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 21 (on “Yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant.”)
quote: A king has not made a covenant with me—that were somewhat; but the Prince of the kings of the earth, Shaddai, the Lord All-sufficient, the Jehovah of ages, the everlasting Elohim, “He hath made with me an everlasting covenant.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 23 (on “Friend, go up higher.”)
quote: When first the life of grace begins in the soul, we do indeed draw near to God, but it is with great fear and trembling. The soul conscious of guilt, and humbled thereby, is overawed with the solemnity of its position; it is cast to the earth by a sense of the grandeur of Jehovah, in whose presence it stands.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 25 (on “Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.”)
quote: Let us today go down to Bethlehem, and in company with wondering shepherds and adoring Magi, let us see him who was born King of the Jews, for we by faith can claim an interest in him, and can sing, “Unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given.”

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 27 (on “Can the rush grow up without mire?”)
quote: A godly man often grows best when his worldly circumstances decay. He who follows Christ for his bag is a Judas; they who follow for loaves and fishes are children of the devil; but they who attend him out of love to himself are his own beloved ones.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 29 (on “Hitherto hath the Lord helped us.”)
quote: We delight to look down a long avenue of trees. It is delightful to gaze from end to end of the long vista, a sort of verdant temple, with its branching pillars and its arches of leaves; even so look down the long aisles of your years, at the green boughs of mercy overhead, and the strong pillars of lovingkindness and faithfulness which bear up your joys.

speaker: Charles H. Spurgeon
title: Morning and Evening, December 31 (on “In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, if any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.”)
quote: “We pray you,” says the Apostle, “as though God did beseech you by us.” What earnest, pathetic terms are these! How deep must be the love which makes the Lord weep over sinners, and like a mother woo his children to his bosom!

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Great Reverence With Which We Should Receive Christ
quote: Oh, the wonderful and hidden grace of this Sacrament which only the faithful of Christ understand, which unbelievers and slaves of sin cannot experience! In it spiritual grace is conferred, lost virtue restored, and the beauty, marred by sin, repaired. At times, indeed, its grace is so great that, from the fullness of the devotion, not only the mind but also the frail body feels filled with greater strength.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Great Reverence With Which We Should Receive Christ
quote: Very great, too, is the difference between the Ark of the Covenant with its treasures and Your most pure Body with its ineffable virtues, between these sacrifices of the law which were but figures of things to come and the true offering of Your Body which was the fulfillment of all ancient sacrifices.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Do Not Lightly Forego Holy Communion
quote: Any devout person may at any hour on any day receive Christ in spiritual communion profitably and without hindrance. Yet on certain days and times appointed he ought to receive with affectionate reverence the Body of his Redeemer in this Sacrament, seeking the praise and honor of God rather than his own consolation.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Do Not Lightly Forego Holy Communion
quote: Do not remain away from Holy Communion because of a small trouble or vexation but go at once to confession and willingly forgive all others their offenses. If you have offended anyone, humbly seek pardon and God will readily forgive you.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Body of Christ and Sacred Scripture Are Most Necessary to a Faithful Soul
quote: Thanks to You, Lord Jesus, Light of eternal light, for the table of Your holy teaching which You have prepared for us by Your servants, the prophets and Apostles and other learned men.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Body of Christ and Sacred Scripture Are Most Necessary to a Faithful Soul
quote: O MOST sweet Lord Jesus, how great is the happiness of the devout soul that feasts upon You at Your banquet, where there is set before her to be eaten no other food but Yourself alone, her only Lover, most desired of all that her heart can desire!

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Communicant Should Prepare Himself for Christ with Great Care
quote: I AM the Lover of purity, the Giver of all holiness. I seek a pure heart and there is the place of My rest.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Communicant Should Prepare Himself for Christ with Great Care
quote: When I grant the grace of devotion, give thanks to God, not because you are worthy but because I have had mercy upon you. If you have it not and feel rather dry instead, continue in prayer, sigh and knock, and do not give up until you receive some crumb of saving grace.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: With All Her Heart the Devout Soul Should Desire Union with Christ in the Sacrament
quote: You truly are the hidden God. Your counsel is not with the wicked, and Your conversation is rather with the humble and the simple.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Grace of Devotion is Acquired Through Humility and Self-Denial
quote: YOU must seek earnestly the grace of devotion, ask for it fervently, await it patiently and hopefully, receive it gratefully, guard it humbly, cooperate with it carefully and leave to God, when it comes, the length and manner of the heavenly visitation.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Grace of Devotion is Acquired Through Humility and Self-Denial
quote: Anyone, therefore, who shall with simplicity of heart direct his intention to God and free himself from all inordinate love or dislike for any creature will be most fit to receive grace and will be worthy of the gift of devotion. For where the Lord finds the vessel empty He pours down His blessing.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: We Should Show Our Needs to Christ and Ask His Grace
quote: What wonder if I were completely inflamed by You to die to myself, since You are the fire ever burning and never dying, a love purifying the heart and enlightening the understanding.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: We Should Show Our Needs to Christ and Ask His Grace
quote: Let Your presence wholly inflame me, consume and transform me into Yourself, that I may become one spirit with You by the grace of inward union and by the melting power of Your ardent love.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Burning Love and Strong Desire to Receive Christ
quote: Accept, O Lord my God, my promises and desires of giving You infinite praise and boundless benediction, which in the vastness of Your ineffable greatness are justly due You. This I render and desire to render every day and every moment of time, and in my loving prayers I invite and entreat all celestial spirits and all the faithful to join me in giving You praise and thanks.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Burning Love and Strong Desire to Receive Christ
quote: WITH greatest devotion and ardent love, with all affection and fervor of heart I wish to receive You, O Lord, as many saints and devout persons, most pleasing to You in their holiness of life and most fervent in devotion, desired You in Holy Communion.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Man Should Not Scrutinize This Sacrament in Curiosity, But Humbly Imitate Christ and Submit Reason to Holy Faith
quote: God can do more than man can understand. A pious and humble search for truth He will allow, a search that is ever ready to learn and that seeks to walk in the reasonable doctrine of the fathers.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Man Should Not Scrutinize This Sacrament in Curiosity, But Humbly Imitate Christ and Submit Reason to Holy Faith
quote: Go forward, then, with sincere and unflinching faith, and with humble reverence approach this Sacrament. Whatever you cannot understand commit to the security of the all-powerful God, Who does not deceive you. The man, however, who trusts in himself is deceived. God walks with sincere men, reveals Himself to humble men, enlightens the understanding of pure minds, and hides His grace from the curious and the proud.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: God’s Great Goodness and Love is Shown to Man in This Sacrament
quote: TRUSTING in Your goodness and great mercy, O Lord, I come as one sick to the Healer, as one hungry and thirsty to the Fountain of life, as one in need to the King of heaven, a servant to his Lord, a creature to his Creator, a soul in desolation to my gentle Comforter.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: God’s Great Goodness and Love is Shown to Man in This Sacrament
quote: Behold, whence love proceeds! What condescension shines forth! What great thanks and praise are due You for these gifts! Oh, how salutary and profitable was Your design in this institution! How sweet and pleasant the banquet when You gave Yourself as food!

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Many Blessings Are Given Those Who Receive Communion Worthily
quote: Whatever is wanting in me, good Jesus, Savior most holy, do You in Your kindness and grace supply for me, You Who have been pleased to call all unto You, saying: “Come to Me all you that labor and are burdened and I will refresh you.”

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Dignity of the Sacrament and of the Priesthood
quote: The priest, indeed, is the minister of God, using the word of God according to His command and appointment. God, moreover, is there—the chief 227 Author and invisible Worker to Whom all is subject as He wills, to Whom all are obedient as He commands.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Dignity of the Sacrament and of the Priesthood
quote: Behold, you have been made a priest, consecrated to celebrate Mass! See to it now that you offer sacrifice to God faithfully and devoutly at proper times, and that you conduct yourself blamelessly. You have not made your burden lighter. Instead, you are now bound by stricter discipline and held to more perfect sanctity.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: The Examination of Conscience and the Resolution to Amend
quote: ABOVE all, God’s priest should approach the celebration and reception of this Sacrament with the deepest humility of heart and suppliant reverence, with complete faith and the pious intention of giving honor to God.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: We Should Offer Ourselves and All That We Have to God, Praying for All
quote: Take away from our hearts, O Lord, all suspicion, anger, wrath, contention, and whatever may injure charity and lessen brotherly love. Have mercy, O Lord, have mercy on those who ask Your mercy, give grace to those who need it, and make us such that we may be worthy to enjoy Your favor and gain eternal life.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: We Should Offer Ourselves and All That We Have to God, Praying for All
quote: Forgive me, O God, forgive me my sins for Your Holy Name. Save my soul which You have redeemed by Your most precious Blood. See, I place myself at Your mercy. I commit myself to Your hands. Deal with me according to Your goodness, not according to my malicious and evil ways.

speaker: Thomas à Kempis
title: Imitating Christ and Despising All Vanities on Earth
quote: The teaching of Christ is more excellent than all the advice of the saints, and he who has His spirit will find in it a hidden manna.
